46: ## Architecture
47: 
48: **QBrainAi** is an ASP.NET Core 9 server (.NET 9.0) providing workspace-scoped context retrieval, TODO management, session logging, repository operations, GraphRAG, and GitHub automation for AI agents.
49: 
50: ### Transports
51: 
52: - **HTTP REST** — Controllers at `/qbrainai/*` in `src/QBrainAi.Support.Mcp/Controllers/`
53: - **MCP Streamable HTTP** — JSON-RPC wire protocol at `/mcp-transport`
54: - **MCP STDIO** — `--transport stdio` flag; tools in `McpStdio/FwhMcpTools.cs`
55: 
56: ### Workspace Model
57: 
58: A single host process manages multiple workspaces. Each workspace gets its own in-process Kestrel `WebApplication` via `WorkspaceAppFactory` (not child processes). The primary workspace is served directly by the host. Workspace targeting uses the `X-Workspace-Path` header. Config lives in `appsettings.yaml` under `Mcp:Workspaces`. Per-instance overrides: `Mcp:Instances:{name}:*` resolved by `McpInstanceResolver`.
59: 
60: ### Search Pipeline
61: 
62: Hybrid search combining SQLite FTS5 full-text with HNSW vector similarity (384-dim all-MiniLM-L6-v2 ONNX embeddings). `HybridSearchService` fuses results with BM25 scoring.
63: 
64: ### Storage
65: 
66: EF Core with SQLite (`McpDbContext`), with migration projects for SQLite, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server. TODO items live in the configured database as the sole source of truth; `docs/Project/TODO.yaml` is a read-only projection. `Mcp:TodoStorage:Provider` accepts `database` (`sqlite` is a deprecated alias; the removed `yaml` value fails fast per TR-MCP-CFG-007).
67: 
68: ### Key Projects
69: 
70: - `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp` — main server application
71: - `QBrainAi.Services` — ingestion, context search, models
72: - `QBrainAi.Storage` — EF Core with SQLite FTS5 + HNSW vector search
73: - `QBrainAi.Cqrs` — CQRS command/query handlers
74: - `QBrainAi.McpAgent` — agent hosting & tool execution framework
75: - `QBrainAi.Client` — typed REST client (published as NuGet `QBrainAI.Client`)
76: - `QBrainAi.GraphRag` — GraphRAG indexing & query (workspace-scoped, disabled by default)
77: - `QBrainAi.Repl.Core` / `QBrainAi.Repl.Host` — REPL command interpreter and dotnet tool
78: 
79: ### Test Projects
80: 
81: - Unit tests: `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Tests`, `QBrainAi.Client.Tests`, `QBrainAi.Cqrs.Tests`, `QBrainAi.Launcher.Tests`, `QBrainAi.McpAgent.Tests`, `QBrainAi.Repl.Core.Tests`
82: - Infrastructure (Nuke build, accountable through TR only; not unit tests, not part of `./build.ps1 Test`): `Build.Tests`
83: - Integration: `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.IntegrationTests`, `QBrainAi.Repl.IntegrationTests`
84: - BDD/Validation (Reqnroll): `QBrainAi.Context.Validation`, `QBrainAi.GitHub.Validation`, `QBrainAi.Repo.Validation`, `QBrainAi.SessionLog.Validation`, `QBrainAi.Todo.Validation`, `QBrainAi.ToolRegistry.Validation`, `QBrainAi.Workspace.Validation`
85: 
86: ## Coding Conventions

88: ### XML Documentation Required
89: 
90: `TreatWarningsAsErrors` and `GenerateDocumentationFile` are enabled globally in `Directory.Build.props`. **All public types and members must have XML doc comments** or the build fails (CS1591). Use `/// <inheritdoc />` for interface implementations. Test classes and methods also require XML docs stating what is tested, what data/fixtures are used, and which requirement IDs are validated.
91: 
92: ### Requirement Traceability
93: 
94: All source files reference FR/TR requirement IDs in doc comments (e.g., `/// <summary>TR-PLANNED-CORE-013: Constructor.</summary>`). When adding new functionality, reference the relevant ID from `docs/Project/Functional-Requirements.md` and `docs/Project/Technical-Requirements.md`. Requirements traceability is validated in CI via `./build.ps1 ValidateTraceability`.
95: 
96: ### Central Package Management
97: 
98: NuGet package versions are centralized in `Directory.Packages.props`. Use `<PackageReference Include="..." />` without `Version` in `.csproj` files.
99: 
100: ### Configuration
101: 
102: Configuration uses YAML format (`appsettings.yaml`) via `NetEscapades.Configuration.Yaml`. Primary config section is `Mcp`.
103:

105: 
106: Use `pwsh.exe` (PowerShell 7+) for all scripts. Do not use `powershell.exe`.

119: ## MCP Session Logging — Mandatory Precondition
120: 
121: **Speed is never more important than following workspace procedures.**
122: 
123: ### Session Start (Run Once Per Session)
124: 
125: 1. **Read `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml`** in the repo root for the current API key, endpoints, and base URL
126: 2. **Bootstrap the required plugin interface** before any state-changing MCP call. For Claude Code, use the `mcpserver-claude-code-plugin` wrapper and its `workflow.*` / `client.*` methods. "Not in the visible tool list" does not mean unavailable; use the documented wrapper invocation form.
127: 3. **Verify marker signature and health** through the required plugin status/bootstrap path. Use direct REST only for read-only diagnosis after the documented plugin path fails.
128: 4. **Review recent session history and current TODOs** through the required plugin only after verification succeeds
129: 5. **POST an initial session log turn** through the required plugin
130: 6. **THEN** begin working on the user's request
131: 
132: If signature verification, `/health`, or nonce verification fails: log `MCP_UNTRUSTED`, continue without the MCP server, and do not probe additional MCP endpoints.
133: 
134: ### Per User Message
135: 
136: 1. POST a new session log turn BEFORE starting work
137: 2. Complete the user's request
138: 3. Update the turn with results, actions taken, and files modified when done
139: 
140: ### Re-run Full Session Start Only If
141: 
142: - The user explicitly says "Start Session"
143: - Signature verification fails
144: - `/health` fails or nonce verification fails
145: - Any `/qbrainai/*` call returns 401
146: - The marker endpoint/key changes after a server restart
147: 
148: ### Authentication
149: 
150: All `/qbrainai/*` endpoints require a per-workspace auth token (from `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml`). These details are for plugin internals, typed client integration, and read-only diagnosis after plugin failure; they are not permission to bypass the required plugin route for session log, TODO, requirements, import/export, or traceability operations:
151: - Header: `X-Api-Key: <token>`
152: - Or query param: `?api_key=<token>`
153: - If you receive a 401, re-read the marker file — the token rotates on each server restart
154: 
155: ### Session Log Rules
156: 
157: - Use rich turn detail: interpretation, response, status, actions (type/status/filePath), contextList, filesModified, designDecisions, requirementsDiscovered, blockers, and key processingDialog
158: - Persist session log updates immediately after each meaningful change — do not defer saves
159: - Before any compaction step, persist the current session log state; after compaction, update again to record the outcome
160: - Agents must identify themselves accurately using their real agent identity in Pascal-Case (e.g., `ClaudeCode`). Do not use placeholder or misleading sourceType values
161: 
162: ### Naming Conventions
163: 
164: - **TODO IDs**: uppercase canonical form `<SDLC-PHASE>-<AREA>-###` (e.g., `PLAN-NAMINGCONVENTIONS-001`) or `ISSUE-{number}`. Never write to `TODO.yaml` directly
165: - **Session IDs**: `<Agent>-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<suffix>` with Pascal-Case agent prefix
166: - **Request IDs**: `req-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<slugOrOrdinal>`, unique within a session

168: ## Agent Conduct
169: 
170: - Do not fabricate information. Acknowledge mistakes. Distinguish facts from speculation
171: - Prioritize correctness over speed. Do not ship code you have not verified compiles
172: - Log every decision to the session log, including: what was decided, why, alternatives considered, what was rejected
173: - Document all web sources as actions with type `web_reference`
174: - Do not use table-style output in responses — use concise bullets or short paragraphs

210: ## QBrain.AI Claude Plugin and Hook Contract
211: 
212: Claude must treat QBrain.AI plugin and hook setup as a live runtime contract, not background documentation. On every new Claude session in this workspace, and whenever QBrain.AI behavior looks stale, incomplete, or inconsistent, perform this validation before relying on QBrain.AI workflows.
213: 
214: ### Required Startup Validation
215: 
216: 1. Read `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` from the active workspace root and use it as the current source of truth for QBrain.AI endpoint, API key, workspace path, plugin instructions, and failure-reporting rules.
217: 2. Identify the active QBrain.AI Claude plugin cache path and version from the marker file, plugin manifest, or active wrapper path. Do not assume a previously cached path is current.
218: 3. Inspect `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\plugins\cache` for stale QBrain.AI plugin entries. Delete stale `mcpserver`, `mcpserver-*`, or `mcpserver-cowork` cache entries that are not the active plugin cache path/version for this session.
219: 4. Do not delete the active plugin cache path for the current session. If unsure which path is active, stop deleting and report the ambiguity.
220: 5. Reload or rebootstrap the active QBrain.AI Claude plugin after stale cache cleanup.
221: 6. Inspect Claude active settings, including user-level and workspace/session-level settings, and verify QBrain.AI hooks are actually installed in the active settings layer. Do not accept hook files existing in the plugin package as proof that hooks are active.
222: 7. If hooks are missing or stale, install or refresh them through the supported QBrain.AI Claude plugin hook validation skill or wrapper path.
223: 8. Verify the plugin wrapper/status command works and record the exact command or tool path used.
224: 9. Verify subprocesses launched by the plugin use the workspace root as process current working directory, not the inherited user profile directory.
225: 
226: ### Required Usage Rules
227: 
228: 1. Use supported QBrain.AI plugin wrappers, hooks, skills, or MCP tools for session logging, TODOs, requirements, triage, and status checks. Do not use raw REST when a supported wrapper, hook, skill, or MCP tool exists.
229: 2. Session logging must use the supported session wrapper or MCP tools and must create, update, and complete turns through the plugin flow.
230: 3. TODO operations must use the supported TODO wrapper, workflow, or MCP tools. Do not edit TODO storage directly.
231: 4. Requirements operations must use the supported requirements wrapper, workflow, or MCP tools. Do not edit requirements storage directly.
232: 5. Triage operations must use the supported triage wrapper, workflow, or MCP tools.
233: 6. QBrain.AI failures and plugin failures discovered while doing unrelated work must always be written as a normal failsafe YAML report through the plugin failsafe flow, then submitted through triage.
234: 7. If triage submission succeeds, Claude must continue the user active task without waiting for triage research or TODO creation. If triage submission fails, stop work and notify the user. Do not invent a raw REST fallback or alternate reporting channel.
235: 8. Normal plugin execution must use PowerShell only. Bash is allowed only for installing PowerShell. Node must not be used for JSON or YAML construction.
236: 9. JSON and YAML payloads must be built from native objects and serialized. Do not handwrite YAML or JSON as fragile string literals.
237: 10. If any validation check fails, report the exact failed check, the path or command involved, and the blocked capability. Do not claim QBrain.AI compliance until the check is fixed or explicitly marked unavailable.
238: 
239: ### Minimum Validation Report
240: 
241: When asked to validate plugin or hook usage, Claude must return a concise report containing:
242: 
243: - Active workspace path.
244: - Marker file path and timestamp.
245: - Active plugin cache path and version.
246: - Stale plugin cache paths deleted.
247: - Hook settings file paths inspected.
248: - Hooks found, installed, or refreshed.
249: - Wrapper/status command used and result.
250: - Session logging validation result.

7: # Requirements Management
8: 
9: ## Overview
10: 
11: To manage functional requirements (FR), technical requirements (TR), test requirements (TEST), and their traceability mappings, use this plugin's declared hook/wrapper (or the REPL transport) for the `workflow.requirements.*` namespace. Do not substitute raw REST calls, generic `PowerShell.MCP wrapper`, helper modules, or another agent's plugin for normal requirements work.
12: 
13: The plugin wrapper validates documented params and emits single-line JSON to REPL stdio. Any direct REPL diagnostic call must use one single-line JSON request envelope, not formatted YAML.
14: 
15: The database is the source of truth for requirements. Markdown files are import/export projections only. Every operation is scoped to the workspace resolved from the signed marker, and generated workspace output must contain only the requested workspace's FR, TR, TEST, and traceability links.
16: 
17: ## Initialization
18: 
19: Call `workflow.sessionlog.bootstrap` through this plugin's declared hook/wrapper to initialize the session log subsystem before issuing any workflow commands. This call is idempotent and should be made once per conversation context.

23: payload:
24:   requestId: req-20260409T120000Z-bootstrap-001
25:   method: workflow.sessionlog.bootstrap
26:   params: {}
27: ```

29: ## Requirement Scope Layers
30: 
31: Plugin version 1.13.0 and newer exposes native layer operations. Treat this section as the layer API reference when plugin status reports these methods; do not ask the operator or inspect wrapper source just to learn the parameter shapes.
32: 
33: - `workflow.requirements.listLayers` / `req_list_layers` / `client.Requirements.ListRequirementLayersAsync`: omit params.
34: - `workflow.requirements.createLayer` / `req_create_layer` / `client.Requirements.CreateRequirementLayerAsync`: required params are `key`, `order`, and `name`; optional params are `description` and `scopeEndLayerKey`.
35: - `workflow.requirements.updateLayer` / `req_update_layer` / `client.Requirements.UpdateRequirementLayerAsync`: required param is `key`; optional params are `name`, `description`, and `scopeEndLayerKey`. Layer `order` is immutable; create a new layer rather than attempting to update `order`.
36: - `workflow.requirements.effective` / `req_effective` / `client.Requirements.GetEffectiveRequirementsAsync`: optional param is `layerKey`; omit `layerKey` to use the active workspace layer.

87: ## Requirement ID Conventions
88: 
89: Three ID spaces are in use:
90: 
91: - **FR** - Functional Requirements: `^FR-[A-Z]+-\d{3}$`, e.g. `FR-MCP-001`, `FR-AUTH-042`
92: - **TR** - Technical Requirements: `^TR-[A-Z]+-[A-Z]+-\d{3}$`, e.g. `TR-MCP-ARCH-001`, `TR-AUTH-SEC-002`
93: - **TEST** - Test Requirements: `^TEST-[A-Z]+-\d{3}$`, e.g. `TEST-MCP-001`, `TEST-AUTH-003`

97: ## Functional Requirements (FR)
98: 
99: ### Listing FRs
100: 
101: To retrieve a filtered list of functional requirements:

104: type: request
105: payload:
106:   requestId: req-20260409T120000Z-listfr-001
107:   method: workflow.requirements.listFr
108:   params:
109:     area: MCP
110:     status: in_progress
111: ```

116: type: result

128:         updatedAt: 2026-04-09T12:00:00Z

134: ### Getting a Single FR
135: 
136: To fetch one functional requirement by ID:
137: 
138: ```yaml
139: type: request
140: payload:
141:   requestId: req-20260409T120001Z-getfr-001
142:   method: workflow.requirements.getFr
143:   params:
144:     id: FR-MCP-001
145: ```

147: ### Creating an FR
148: 
149: To record a new functional requirement:
150: 
151: ```yaml
152: type: request
153: payload:
154:   requestId: req-20260409T120002Z-createfr-001
155:   method: workflow.requirements.createFr
156:   params:
157:     id: FR-MCP-003
158:     title: Context search
159:     description: System must support semantic search across workspace documents
160:     priority: high
161:     area: MCP
162:     notes: Use hybrid search combining BM25 and vector embeddings
163: ```
164: 
165: Required fields: `id`, `title`, `description`, `priority`, `area`. The `notes` field is optional.
166: 
167: ### Acceptance Criteria
168: 
169: FR, TR, and TEST create/update commands accept structured `acceptanceCriteria` entries with the same shape used by TODO execution criteria:
170: 
171: ```yaml
172: method: workflow.requirements.createFr
173: params:
174:   id: FR-MCP-XXX-001
175:   title: Acceptance criteria example
176:   description: Requirement records preserve structured pass/fail criteria.
177:   priority: high
178:   area: MCP
179:   acceptanceCriteria:
180:     - id: ac-1
181:       text: Round-trip preserves criterion text
182:       isSatisfied: false
183:     - id: ac-2
184:       text: Evidence is retained when supplied
185:       isSatisfied: true
186:       evidence: tests/Services/RequirementAcceptanceCriteriaTests.cs
187: ```
188: 
189: To copy criteria from an execution TODO onto a requirement, call `workflow.requirements.copyAcceptanceCriteriaFromTodo`:
190: 
191: ```yaml
192: method: workflow.requirements.copyAcceptanceCriteriaFromTodo
193: params:
194:   kind: fr
195:   id: FR-MCP-XXX-001
196:   todoId: PLAN-MCP-001
197: ```
198: 
199: This maps to `POST /mcpserver/requirements/{kind}/{id}/acceptance-criteria/copy-from-todo` with body `{ "todoId": "PLAN-MCP-001" }`.
200: 
201: ### Batch Create Or Update
202: 
203: When creating or updating multiple records, prefer the atomic batch commands instead of Markdown ingestion. Batch commands accept YAML `records:` arrays and fail all records if any record is invalid, conflicts, or is missing during update.
204: 
205: Use per-kind commands when every record is the same type:
206: 
207: ```yaml
208: type: request
209: payload:
210:   requestId: req-20260409T120002Z-createfr-batch-001
211:   method: workflow.requirements.createFrBatch
212:   params:
213:     records:
214:       - id: FR-MCP-004
215:         title: Batch requirements
216:         description: The system must accept multiple requirement records in one request.
217:         priority: high
218:       - id: FR-MCP-005
219:         title: Atomic validation
220:         description: The system must reject the whole batch when one record is invalid.

24: ## 2. Goals and non-goals
25: 
26: Goals:
27: 
28: 1. A durable HV queue whose admission, scheduling, ownership, and finalization survive server restarts, worker crashes, and concurrent workers without losing or duplicating a review result.
29: 2. A reviewer pool of five agents (Cline, Copilot, Claude, Codex, Grok), selected round-robin among the ready reviewers, never the submitter, the agent that wrote the reviewed turns, or an alias of either.
30: 3. Complete evidence: the complete accepted request and the complete response log of every review, compressed at rest with GZIP, verified lossless, retained until explicitly removed, and streamed live while the review runs.
31: 4. Per-turn assessments and a separate holistic evaluation for every request, committed atomically with the turns' hostile reviews; reviewed turns and final results are immutable.
32: 5. Independence: an agent's self-review never affects HV admission, execution, or verdict, and an HV verdict never completes a TODO.
33: 
34: Non-goals (each settled by the operator, section 3): access roles; a force re-review flag; automatic TODO state changes; automatic retention expiry; execution time limits; a second HV verdict store beside this one for turn reviews.

139: ## 5. Design decisions and resolutions
140: 
141: Each resolution names the settled requirements it implements, its rationale, and the alternatives it rejects. Resolutions are proposals for the operator's approval; the settled requirements of section 3 are not reopened.
142: 
143: - R-01 One bounded context. HostileValidation owns the pipeline and is not gated by `Mcp:AgentContext:Mode`: HV of turns works in every Mode, because the operator's HV requirements (S-01 to S-30) name turns, not agent-context responses. Rejected: extending the foundation's `AgentContextHvRequest` in ResponsesAndTrust (draft 103), because that record is mode-gated (foundation section 3.5.1) and lists responses, not turns, so a turn with no response would silently drop out of review (draft 213, "turn coverage versus response coverage").
144: - R-02 The HV request replaces the foundation's agent-context HV request. `HvRequest` keeps the foundation's key format `hvr-<sessionId>-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>` (with `-<nn>` from the second key of one second, ReadableKeyAllocator) and lists turns (`HvRequestTurn`); the agent responses of those turns are linked as `HvRequestResponse` items when Phase C has recorded any. CreateAgentContextHvRequestCommand, GetAgentContextHvRequestQuery, QueryAgentContextHvRequestsQuery, and their entities are superseded (amendment A-04). Rejected: keeping two HV request records (one per turn, one per response), which would need a cross-record consistency rule the foundation never needed.
145: - R-03 Model grades come from finalization only. FinalizeHvRequestCommand dispatches the foundation's RecordModelGradeCommand for each linked response inside its own transaction; the public model-grade route, the two-step `codex exec resume` protocol, and `ModelGrader:*` are removed, and the eight receipt checks become the verification steps V-1 to V-8 of policy HvFinalVerification against evidence the server itself captured (amendment A-05). Rationale: the pipeline launches the reviewer and records its complete output, so the server no longer has to trust receipts written by a runner it did not control. Rejected: keeping the reviewer-submitted grade route beside the pipeline, which would let a grade bypass reviewer exclusion and atomic finalization (S-17, S-23).
146: - R-04 Freeze at admission, finality at finalization (S-06, S-07). Admission sets each member turn's HV state to `Pending` in the same transaction that creates the request; finalization sets it to `Final`. Every write to a `Pending` or `Final` turn or its children, from every surface and origin, is refused with 409 `turn_immutable` and `details.reason` `hv_pending` or `hv_final` (policy HvTurnFreeze), except the one write of finalization itself (origin `HvFinalization`). A request that ends `Canceled` or `Failed` releases its turns back to `None`. Rationale: the reviewed content equals the finalized content without a content comparison race, and the operator's "may not allow updates" is one guard in the existing write path. Rejected: letting writes continue and refusing finalization on a changed snapshot hash, which would waste completed reviews and still leave a window between the last check and the commit.
147: - R-05 Only terminal turns are admitted. A member turn that is not terminal (`TurnStatus.IsTerminal`, foundation section 3.5.3) refuses the whole request with 409 `hv_turns_not_terminal`, naming each turn. The submitting turn is never a member: a session scope excludes it and reports the exclusion in the result, and a turn or range scope that names it is refused with 400 `hv_scope_includes_submitting_turn` (the foundation's rule that "the request's own turn is never a candidate, a dependency, or cited evidence", foundation section 3.1). A Code or Docs turn that needs HV before it can complete is completed first with `hostileReview` `Other` (for example "HV requested hvr-..."), which the foundation already allows and never counts as an AGREE (foundation C8); finalization then replaces that `Other` with the HV result. Rationale: no turn changes status after it is frozen, so there is no close-inside-finalization path. Rejected: admitting in-progress turns with a declared close intent (draft 213, section 3.B), which adds a mechanism and still freezes a turn the model is working in.
148: - R-06 Hostile reviews are written only by the pipeline. On agent surfaces a `hostileReview` write may carry only `status` `Other` (with its required `otherNotes`); a write naming `Pass`, `Fail`, or `Running`, or carrying `hvVerdict`, is refused with 403 `review_hostile_pipeline_only` (amendment A-06). Process ConvertHvReceiptToReview is retired. Rationale: a manual Pass or Fail would bypass reviewer exclusion, complete evidence, and atomic finalization, and no surface may bypass them (draft 213, H5, adopted). Rejected: keeping the manual route for emergencies; a reviewer can be enabled and checked instead (S-27).
149: - R-07 Assignment at admission, durable round-robin. The submit transaction picks the next eligible reviewer after the workspace's round-robin cursor and advances the cursor in the same SerializableWrite (policy RoundRobinAssignment), so assignment survives restarts and two concurrent submissions never pick from the same cursor value. When the assigned reviewer is no longer eligible at claim time (offline, disabled), the claim reassigns through the same policy and records the reassignment. Rejected: assignment at claim only, which hides the assignee from the submitter and lets claim order, not round-robin order, pick reviewers.
150: - R-08 One agent identity, server-attributed. `AgentIdentity` (namespace `QBrainAi.Client.Agents`, shared by the server, the REPL, and, through the golden contract, the PowerShell core) maps every known alias to one of the five reviewer ids: Claude (`claude`, `claudecode`, `claude-code`, `claudecowork`, `claude-cowork`, `cowork`), Codex (`codex`), Copilot (`copilot`), Grok (`grok`, `grokcode`, `grok-code`, `grokbot`, `grok-bot`), Cline (`cline`, `cline-v2`, `clinev2`), case-insensitively and ignoring separators. The submitter is the agent of the submitting turn, located by its full turn key (TurnLocator); a free-text name never overrides it. The author is the agent of the reviewed session (one request names turns of one MCP session, R-26), stored normalized as `AuthorReviewerId`. A reviewer whose id equals the submitter's or the author's is never eligible (S-17, S-28, P-01, P-07). Develop holds three alias maps with different canonical forms (`src/QBrainAi.Repl.Host/MarkerFileClientOptionsResolver.cs:64-81`, `src/QBrainAi.Repl.Core/TodoSelectionStore.cs:166-171`, the plugin's `Get-ReplCanonicalAgentName`); they are context under the DRY ruling and are not changed by this amendment. Exclusion is by agent family, not by model vendor (D-01, settled): S-17 names "the agent submitting the review", P-01 constrains the agent family and asks separately for the agent and the model, and the operator runs Cline on `gpt-6-astra` (provider `openai-codex`, VI-01 receipt) while keeping Cline and Codex as two reviewers (S-02); a model a reviewer shares with the submitter stays visible in the run's provenance, and the operator can disable that reviewer (UpdateHvReviewerCommand). Exclusion covers the author as well as the submitter (D-05, settled): a review by the agent that wrote the turns is a self-review, which S-28 rules out of HV and P-07 rules out of validation.
151: - R-09 Operator submissions. A caller with no session-log turn (Director, an operator at the REPL) submits with `submitter.kind` `Operator` and a name; no reviewer is excluded for the submitter, and the author of the reviewed session is still excluded (R-08). Agent surfaces (plugin verbs, MCP tools, the REPL workflow verb) always send the submitting turn's key, which the plugin binds automatically (foundation process BindVerbToTurn). Limit (section 8): every caller holds the same workspace key, so the server cannot prove that an `Operator` submission did not come from an agent.
152: - R-10 Readiness through NONCE (S-15, S-27). A reviewer is `Unverified`, `Online`, or `Offline`, and separately enabled or disabled. "NONCE the agent" is a probe run of the reviewer through its adapter with a fresh random nonce: it passes when the reviewer answers with the probe record that echoes the nonce and the adapter's runtime provenance shows the reviewer's resolved model and effort (P-04). Only a passing NONCE moves a reviewer to `Online`. An execution failure moves it to `Offline` until a later NONCE passes. The worker host NONCEs at startup every enabled `Unverified` reviewer whose current configuration has no settled probe, and a configuration change requests a NONCE of the new configuration; an `Offline` reviewer, and an `Unverified` one whose probe of its current configuration is already settled (for example by a server fault), is NONCEd only when a caller asks (S-15: "until resolved"). Every probe ends through one policy, HvProbeOutcome (section 15), whichever unit ends it, and that policy first checks that the probe ran the reviewer's current configuration, so a probe of an older configuration never changes the reviewer. Rejected: a liveness ping or the server health nonce, which S-27 rules out.
153: - R-11 No execution time limit (P-02). A run has no timeout and no deadline. Liveness is the worker's lease, renewed by heartbeats; a stalled run stays visible (`lastOutputUtc`, the last progress record) and anyone can cancel it (S-18). The only expiry is the lease of a dead worker (R-13). This replaces the 30-minute `ExecutionTimeout` of the separate HostileReview options (`src/QBrainAi.Services/Options/HostileReviewWorkerOptions.cs:45-46`, read by nothing today, P1) for HV runs and for the HostileReview worker of section 16.7, whose artifact reviews have no time limit either (P-02). The process exit code is never the outcome of a run: the reviewer's records decide it (V-8 for a review, policy ReadinessProbeVerdict for a probe), because a CLI can end a refused or empty run with exit code 0 (VI-03: a headless Grok run whose write call was refused ended `cancelled` with exit 0, and two Copilot permission variants exited 0 with no output).
154: - R-12 True live output (S-22, P8). Each reviewer adapter delivers every output line as the process writes it, through a line callback, never after the process ends; the worker appends lines in batches (at most `OutputFlushInterval`, default 250 ms, or `OutputFlushBytes`, default 64 KiB, whichever comes first) through AppendHvRunOutputCommand, which stores each batch as one GZIP chunk and wakes the streams. The output stream replays stored chunks and then follows new ones (shared component OrderedEventReplay). Develop's one-shot strategy yields its output only after completion (`src/QBrainAi.Services/Services/OneShotCliAgentExecutionStrategy.cs:57-75`), so the adapters need a real line path (section 21, P8). Acceptance criterion FR-MCP-HVPIPE-008-AC003 makes the difference testable: a line is observable on the stream while the reviewer process is still running. The reviewer's records are read from each agent message's complete text, assembled from the CLI's native events (Grok's `streaming-json` sends message text one token per event, and Copilot sends deltas and then the whole message, as the probe runs of 2026-10-16 show), by one extraction function that the worker runs as lines arrive and finalization runs over the stored log (section 16.3), so a record split across events is read exactly once and both read the same records (FR-MCP-HVPIPE-010-AC006).
155: - R-13 Leases and fences (handoff requirement 10). A run is owned through a lease (owner, expiry) and a fence token that increases on every claim and takeover, the pattern develop already uses for handoff ingestion (owner and expiry with a `StateVersion` takeover, `src/QBrainAi.Services/Services/HandoffIngestionService.cs:724-735`, and a fenced terminal write that matches owner and version, `:782-807`). Every worker write carries the fence; a write with a stale fence changes nothing and returns `stale_fence`, and the worker that receives it stops its process. Expired leases are swept (ExpireHvRunLeasesCommand): the attempt becomes `Abandoned` and the request is queued again until `MaxAttemptsPerRequest` (default 3) is spent, then `Failed`, or `Canceled` when a cancel was requested; policy HvRetryDecision writes that outcome, with its turn release and its notification, for the sweep exactly as for FailHvRunCommand. Rejected: the unused lease options of the HostileReview subsystem (`HostileReviewWorkerOptions.cs:30-46`), which no code reads (section 21, P1).
156: - R-14 Evidence in the relational store, GZIP at rest (S-13, S-29, S-30). The accepted request is one GZIP blob written at admission; the response log is the run's ordered GZIP chunks; the result document is one GZIP blob written at finalization. No uncompressed copy of an evidence item is stored in the evidence tables, and each evidence item is stored there once (the structured rows of section 12, such as the request's `Context` and the findings, are records the units derive, not copies of the evidence blobs). The audit ledger keeps its own history of every evidence write, as it does for every audited entity: develop's ledger snapshots every property of an audited entity, binary columns included (`src/QBrainAi.Storage/McpDbContext.cs:1540-1589`), compressed with GZIP (`src/QBrainAi.Storage/Entities/DataAuditLogEntity.cs:119-147`), and a removal never changes it (R-20, I-13). Retrieval returns `application/gzip` (download name `<hvRequestId>-<kind>.jsonl.gz` or `.json.gz`) or, when asked, the decompressed bytes. The pattern is develop's audit ledger, which stores GZIP payloads in the database (`src/QBrainAi.Storage/Entities/DataAuditLogEntity.cs:66-147`). Rationale: S-23 ("Single trx at end") and S-29 (the database audit log) both hold only when the evidence is in the same transactional store as the result, and no crash window between a file system and the database remains. Rejected: `.jsonl.gz` files beside the database, which would need a two-store protocol, keep evidence outside the audit ledger, and split backups.
157: - R-15 Atomic finalization (S-23). FinalizeHvRequestCommand verifies the evidence and the reviewer output before it opens a transaction, then commits in one SerializableWrite: the result document, the per-turn assessments, the holistic evaluation, the failures, each turn's `hostileReview` through policy HvVerdictMapping (origin `HvFinalization`), each turn's `Final` HV state, the linked responses' model grades and trust decisions (when Mode is not `Off`), the request's `Completed` state, its notification, and the audit rows. The transaction re-checks everything the earlier reads relied on (the run's fence, the chunk manifest, the request and turn states). Crash windows are in section 9.
158: - R-16 Transactional notification outbox (S-19). Every state change that callers observe writes an `HvNotification` row in its own transaction, numbered by a per-workspace sequence that the same transaction advances, so the sequence has no gaps and no row is visible before its change commits. The notification stream replays rows after the caller's `Last-Event-ID` and then follows new ones (OrderedEventReplay). Delivery is at least once; consumers deduplicate by sequence. `IChangeEventBus` (develop's in-memory bus, `src/QBrainAi.Services/Notifications/IChangeEventBus.cs:4`) is used only to wake waiting streams and the worker, never as the record.
159: - R-17 Incidents through the triage endpoint (S-15, S-26). An execution failure writes an `HvIncident` row in the failure's transaction; FileHvIncidentCommand then submits it through `ITriageService` with its `dedupeKey` (`hv-reviewer-<reviewerId>-<failureCode>` for a failure attributable to the reviewer, `hv-server-<failureCode>` otherwise, section 12), which triage groups as `dedupe:<key>` (`src/QBrainAi.Services/Services/TriageService.cs:1475-1476`), and records the returned report and group ids. A filing that fails stays `Pending` and is retried by the worker host's sweep. Rejected: new incident tables with their own deduplication (S-26: "File through endpoint").
160: - R-18 Honest ETA (S-18, P-03). The ETA a caller sees is the reviewer's own latest progress record (`percentComplete`, `etaSeconds`), with `etaStatus` `Reported` and the record's time; with no progress record it is `etaStatus` `Unknown` and no number. The server never estimates.
161: - R-19 Audit participation and hard stop (S-29). Every HV entity carries `IsDeleted`, so `McpDbContext` writes its ledger rows for every HV mutation in the same `SaveChanges` (develop audits only entities with that property, `src/QBrainAi.Storage/McpDbContext.cs:1620-1627`). The ledger is append-only for HV: no HV unit or process updates or deletes a ledger row (I-13). Because develop skips the ledger when the audit table is unavailable (`McpDbContext.cs:1507-1538`), every HV unit first calls the shared component AuditLedgerGuard, which refuses with 503 `audit_unavailable` and writes nothing when the ledger cannot be written. Every evidence read, by a public surface or by the server itself, passes one boundary, AuditLedgerGuard `RecordRead`, which writes an explicit `read` ledger row and commits it on its own before any byte is returned or consumed, never inside the reader's write transaction, so no later rollback of the reader's own writes can erase the record of a read that happened; a read whose row cannot be written is refused (the "protected-log access" of draft 213 participates in the audit log, S-29). The public readers are GetHvEvidenceQuery, GetHvResultQuery, the output stream, and GetHvRequestQuery when it returns output lines, directly or for a same-key replay of SubmitHvRequestCommand; the internal readers are RunReviewerProcess (the accepted request it puts in the brief), FinalizeHvRequestCommand (the run's chunks it verifies), and CloseHvRunOutputCommand (a probe's chunks for policy ReadinessProbeVerdict); each internal reader reads before it opens its write transaction and re-checks in that transaction that the stored state is the one it read.
162: - R-20 Retention until removal (S-29). No unit deletes, expires, or compacts HV evidence except RemoveHvEvidenceCommand, an explicit call that removes the evidence bytes of one request, keeps its result rows, hashes, and sizes, records who removed it and why, and is audited. It clears the evidence tables only and never changes or deletes an audit ledger row: the ledger keeps the history of the evidence's writes and gains the record of the removal, because an audit log is never purged (I-13). There are no roles: any caller with the workspace key can call it, as S-29 requires.
163: - R-21 Self-review independence (S-28). No HV unit, policy, or process reads `agentReview`. The turn snapshot sent to a reviewer omits both review records (shared component TurnSnapshotBuilder), so a reviewer never sees a self-review grade. S-12 (a plugin list of missing agent reviews) is met by the foundation's Stop-gate remedy, which already lists each open turn's missing `agentReview` (foundation section 3.4, Stop gate, and `Get-CloseRemedy`, section 3.5.6), and is not an HV input. Reconciliation with the foundation's completion gate: HV admits only terminal turns (R-05), and the foundation's gate needs an `agentReview` status of `Pass`, `Fail`, or `Other` before a turn can close `completed` (foundation section 5.3, CompletionPolicy); that is a rule of closing a turn, not of HV, it is met by `Other` with a note as well as by a grade, and a turn closed `failed` or `canceled` needs no agent review at all; HV admission, execution, and verdict read none of it, and FR-MCP-HVPIPE-013 proves that every terminal turn is admitted and judged identically whatever its self-review.
164: - R-22 Verdict only (S-25). No HV unit writes TODO state. A result names the reviewed turns' `todoId` values for information only.
165: - R-23 Requirement references (S-14). The submitted context is stored as written (Markdown, YAML, or text, declared by `contextFormat`) and parsed for requirement references: FR, TR, and TEST ids of the form `<KIND>-<AREA>-<NNN>` with optional further dash-separated area segments, acceptance criteria written as `<FR id>-AC<NNN>` or `<FR id> ac-<n>`, and use cases by their store id or exact title. Each reference is resolved against the workspace's effective requirements and use cases and handed to the reviewer as a delineated list with its resolution status; an unresolved reference is listed as unresolved, never refused (shared component RequirementReferenceExtractor).
166: - R-24 The reviewer's own turn (P-06). The brief tells the reviewer to log its review as its own session-log turn, classified `Chore` so that its turn never needs an HV of its own (foundation completion policy: Chore needs no hostile review), and to store its entire result there. Finalization requires that turn to exist, to be persisted (not a failsafe or queued record), to have been created at or after the run's claim, to be closed `completed` as a `Chore`, and to contain every reviewer record of the run byte for byte in its stored normal form (V-6). A reviewer whose host cannot log turns fails its NONCE with `reviewer_turn_logging_unsupported`. The reviewer's plugin runs as a host session of its own: a review or probe run never reads or changes the plugin state or the session-log session of a live session of the same agent in the workspace (FR-MCP-HVPIPE-008-AC008), which matters because a reviewer starts in the workspace (section 16.2) and Grok's headless hooks write their host state under the working directory's `.mcpServer/grok/` (VI-04).
167: - R-25 The HostileReview subsystem stays separate. FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-001 to -006 (its queue, artifact links, findings, and query surface) are not changed by this amendment, as the foundation already states (foundation section 5.4); the problems found in it (section 21, P1 to P3) are tracked in REMED-HVPIPELINE-001. It stays separate (D-02, settled): it reviews artifacts (TODO, FR/TR/TEST, plans, files, commits; FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-002) while this pipeline reviews session turns (S-03), the approved foundation keeps it separate, and consolidating it is scope the operator has not named. Its missing worker (P1) has its own contract (section 16.7) and shares only the execution primitives that fit it (the reviewer adapters' launch builder, live-line path, containment, and provenance reader, and FencedLease), so reviewer execution exists once (the DRY ruling); nothing of this pipeline's evidence model applies to it, because FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-002 forbids storing a raw artifact or an assembled prompt.
168: - R-26 Scope limits. One request names turns of one MCP session. `MaxTurnsPerRequest` (default 200, the foundation's `HvRequest:MaxTurns` default) bounds every scope; a session scope above it is refused with 400 `hv_scope_too_large` naming the count, never truncated.
169: - R-27 One open review per turn. A turn is `Pending` in at most one open request (a unique filtered index on the turn key where the item is `Pending`); admission over a pending turn is refused with 409 `hv_turns_pending` naming the turns and their requests, and over a final turn with 409 `hv_turns_already_reviewed` (S-06, S-20).
170: - R-28 Cancellation by anyone (S-18). `Queued` becomes `Canceled` at once; `Running` becomes `CancelRequested`, and the worker stops the process at its next heartbeat and closes the run `Canceled`; a repeat on a `CancelRequested` or `Canceled` request returns 200 unchanged; `Finalizing`, `Completed`, and `Failed` refuse with 409 `hv_request_not_cancelable`. A cancel, a close, and a finalization of the same request are serialized on the request row, so exactly one of them commits first and the others see its state: a close that finds `CancelRequested` ends the run `Canceled` instead of making the request `Finalizing`, so an accepted cancellation is never lost (CloseHvRunOutputCommand).
171: - R-29 Worker units are internal. ClaimHvRunCommand, RecordHvRunStartCommand, RecordHvRunHeartbeatCommand, AppendHvRunOutputCommand, CloseHvRunOutputCommand, FailHvRunCommand, ExpireHvRunLeasesCommand, FinalizeHvRequestCommand, and FileHvIncidentCommand have no REST route, MCP tool, or client method; only the worker host dispatches them, in-process, through `IDispatcher`. The public mutations are submit, cancel, reviewer update, NONCE, and evidence removal.
172: - R-30 Plugins consume notifications through the REPL. Plugins never call REST (foundation section 3); the REPL gains a streaming verb that follows the notification stream, and the PowerShell core runs it in the background per host session (process WatchHvNotifications), keeping the last sequence and the inbox in one state file of the host session, so one atomic replace records both, and handing completions of requests that host session's MCP session submitted to the next prompt as context. A terminal notification carries the submitter's turn key (section 12), so the watcher matches it by that key and needs no local record of the submission, and a completion that arrives before the submit verb has returned is still delivered. Delivery to the model is at least once: a crash between adding a completion to a prompt and recording it delivered can repeat it, and each entry carries its sequence so a repeat is recognizable (the outbox rule of R-16).
173: - R-31 The 98/98 bar for the overall verdict (P-05), one predicate stated once here. The overall verdict is `AGREE` exactly when all of these hold: the holistic correctness and completeness both meet `max(configured hostile threshold, 0.98)` (ScoreVerdict, foundation section 3.5.4) and the holistic verdict is `AGREE`; every member turn's verdict is `AGREE`; every response grade of the accepted request is `AGREE` under the foundation's `verdict_match` rule; and no finding of any scope (turn, holistic, or response) is FAIL or UNKNOWN. Otherwise it is `DISAGREE`. The predicate reads only the reviewed inputs, which do not change: the response grades are those of every response admitted with the request (section 13.3), including one whose response has since left the review (its item `Closed`), because the reviewer graded what was admitted and emitted its verdict over it; a later state change of a response decides only whether its grade is applied (section 14.4), never the overall verdict. Per-turn hostile reviews keep the foundation's configured hostile thresholds through HvVerdictMapping. V-4 checks the reviewer's overall verdict against this predicate, and finalization stores the same value.

192: ## 7. Lifecycles
193: 
194: ### 7.1 HV request
195: 
196: ```mermaid
197: stateDiagram-v2
198:     [*] --> Queued: SubmitHvRequestCommand, turns frozen Pending
199:     Queued --> Running: ClaimHvRunCommand, run attempt claimed
200:     Queued --> Canceled: CancelHvRequestCommand
201:     Running --> Queued: attempt Failed or Abandoned, attempts left
202:     Running --> CancelRequested: CancelHvRequestCommand
203:     CancelRequested --> Canceled: worker stops the process, the run closes or fails, or the lease expires
204:     Running --> Finalizing: CloseHvRunOutputCommand, output closed
205:     Finalizing --> Completed: FinalizeHvRequestCommand commits, turns Final
206:     Finalizing --> Queued: verification failed, attempts left
207:     Running --> Failed: attempts spent
208:     Finalizing --> Failed: verification failed, attempts spent
209:     Canceled --> [*]: turns released to None
210:     Failed --> [*]: turns released to None
211:     Completed --> [*]
212: ```
213: 
214: - `Queued` and `Running` hold the turns `Pending`. `Completed`, `Failed`, and `Canceled` are terminal and never change again (S-06, S-20). A request whose attempt fails returns to `Queued` with its assignment re-evaluated (R-07); with no eligible reviewer it stays `Queued`, its ETA `Unknown`, until a reviewer passes a NONCE or the request is canceled, so no work is lost to an outage.
215: - `CancelRequested` is not terminal: the request is canceled when the worker has stopped the process, when its run closes or fails first (CloseHvRunOutputCommand and FailHvRunCommand through policy HvRetryDecision, R-28), or when the lease of a dead worker expires.
216: 
217: ### 7.2 Run attempt
218: 
219: ```mermaid
220: stateDiagram-v2
221:     [*] --> Claimed: ClaimHvRunCommand, lease and fence
222:     Claimed --> Running: RecordHvRunStartCommand, process started
223:     Running --> Running: heartbeat renews the lease, output appended
224:     Running --> OutputClosed: CloseHvRunOutputCommand
225:     Claimed --> Failed: FailHvRunCommand, process never started, or worker_shutdown
226:     Running --> Failed: FailHvRunCommand, execution failure
227:     Running --> Canceled: cancel observed at a heartbeat
228:     OutputClosed --> Canceled: cancel found at close
229:     Claimed --> Abandoned: lease expired, ExpireHvRunLeasesCommand
230:     Running --> Abandoned: lease expired, ExpireHvRunLeasesCommand
231:     OutputClosed --> Succeeded: FinalizeHvRequestCommand committed, or probe passed
232:     OutputClosed --> Failed: verification failed, or probe failed
233:     Succeeded --> [*]
234:     Failed --> [*]
235:     Abandoned --> [*]
236:     Canceled --> [*]
237: ```
238: 
239: A run is either a `Review` run of an HV request or a `Probe` run of a reviewer's NONCE (R-10); both use the same lease, fence, output, and close units, so the probe needs no second execution path.

241: ### 7.3 Reviewer readiness
242: 
243: ```mermaid
244: stateDiagram-v2
245:     [*] --> Unverified: seeded from configuration
246:     Unverified --> Online: NONCE probe passed
247:     Unverified --> Offline: NONCE probe failed
248:     Online --> Offline: execution failure, incident filed
249:     Offline --> Online: NONCE probe passed
250:     Online --> Unverified: strategy, agent path, model, or effort changed
251:     Offline --> Unverified: strategy, agent path, model, or effort changed
252: ```
253: 
254: `Enabled` is a separate flag set by UpdateHvReviewerCommand: a disabled reviewer is never eligible and is never NONCEd automatically, whatever its readiness. Eligibility (policy HvReviewerEligibility) is enabled, `Online`, and neither the submitter nor the author of the reviewed turns (R-08).

256: ### 7.4 HV state of a turn
257: 
258: ```mermaid
259: stateDiagram-v2
260:     [*] --> None
261:     None --> Pending: admitted by SubmitHvRequestCommand
262:     Pending --> None: request Canceled or Failed
263:     Pending --> Final: FinalizeHvRequestCommand
264:     Final --> [*]
265: ```
266: 
267: While `Pending` or `Final`, policy HvTurnFreeze refuses every write to the turn and its children except finalization's own (A-07, A-08). A turn that already holds a `Pass` or `Fail` hostile review when the column is added starts `Final`, with no request id (A-11).

269: ## 8. Invariants and limits
270: 
271: Invariants, each owned by the named component and proved by the acceptance criteria of section 19:
272: 
273: - I-01 A turn is `Pending` in at most one open request, and a `Final` turn is never admitted again (R-27, HvAdmissionEligibility).
274: - I-02 The content a reviewer reviewed is the content finalized: no write reaches a `Pending` turn between admission and finalization (HvTurnFreeze), and finalization re-hashes each turn's snapshot and refuses on any difference (V-2).
275: - I-03 A request is finalized at most once; a second finalization returns the stored result and writes nothing (FinalizeHvRequestCommand).
276: - I-04 Nothing of a finalization is visible unless all of it is: result, per-turn assessments, holistic evaluation, failures, turn reviews, turn finality, grades, trust decisions, request state, notification, and audit rows commit together (R-15, S-23).
277: - I-05 Only the run that holds the current fence can append output, close output, or fail; a stale fence changes nothing (R-13).
278: - I-06 The response log of a finalized run is complete: its chunks are contiguous from sequence 1, each chunk's SHA-256 matches its decompressed bytes, the chain hash over the chunks' SHA-256 values equals the run's `OutputChainSha256` (section 12), every line parses as one JSON object, and the log contains exactly one `hv_verdict` record (V-1).
279: - I-07 The reviewer is never the submitter or the author of the reviewed turns, by canonical id (V-5, R-08).
280: - I-08 Varying a turn's `agentReview` (absent, any status, any score) changes neither admission, nor assignment, nor the brief's bytes, nor the verdict mapping (R-21).
281: - I-09 No HV unit changes TODO state (R-22).
282: - I-10 No HV write happens without its audit ledger rows (R-19).
283: - I-11 Evidence bytes are removed from the evidence tables only by RemoveHvEvidenceCommand (R-20).
284: - I-12 Every notification row is committed with the change it reports, and sequences are gap-free per workspace (R-16).
285: - I-13 The audit ledger is append-only: no HV unit or process updates or deletes a ledger row, and a removal of evidence leaves every earlier ledger row unchanged (R-19, R-20).
286: 
287: Limits stated plainly:
288: 
289: - L-01 Agent identity rests on the workspace key: every caller holds the same key, so the server cannot prove which agent sent a request. Exclusion is enforced against the agent of the submitting turn the server finds and the agent of the reviewed session; an `Operator` submission excludes only the author (R-09). This is the foundation's existing identity model (foundation section 6.3: "every agent of a workspace authenticates with the workspace key"), not a new weakness.
290: - L-02 A reviewer can run more than once for one request (at-least-once execution): a worker crash after the reviewer finished but before its output was closed leads to a new attempt. The request still finalizes at most once (I-03), and every attempt's output stays as evidence.
291: - L-03 Incident deduplication is per triage group: a filing retried after a crash between the triage commit and the recording of its report id can add a second report to the same group, never a second group (R-17).
292: - L-04 A reviewer CLI that cannot report its runtime model and effort cannot pass a NONCE, so it stays `Unverified` or `Offline` (R-10, P-04). Verified on 2026-10-16 (VI-01): Codex, Claude, Grok, and Copilot record both in their own run records; Cline records the model and only whether thinking was on, never the effort level, so Cline cannot pass a NONCE until it records the effort of a run (D-06, settled: P-04 fails closed).

294: ## 9. Crash windows and recovery
295: 
296: Each window names what is durable at the crash and what recovers it. "Sweep" is the worker host's periodic pass (process HvWorkerHost).
297: 
298: - W-01 Crash after the submit commit, before the worker wakes: the request is `Queued` in the store; the next poll claims it.

329: ### 11.1 FencedLease (namespace `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Storage.Leases`)
330: 
331: Claims, renews, and takes over the lease of one row, and guards every fenced write, following develop's handoff-ingestion pattern (`HandoffIngestionService.cs:724-735,782-807`). Operations: `Claim(row, owner, duration)` (only when the row has no lease or an expired one; the fence token increments), `Renew(row, owner, fence, duration)`, `Guard(row, owner, fence)` (the precondition of every fenced write), `Release(row, owner, fence)`, and `Expire(row, fence, liveStatuses)` (a sweep's takeover of a dead worker's row: in the caller's transaction the row must still be in one of the live statuses, with the fence the sweep read and an expired lease; otherwise the result is `skipped` and nothing changes, because the row was renewed, settled, or already taken over; when it holds, the fence token increments and owner and expiry are cleared, so the dead worker's next write is `stale_fence` and no second sweep can take the same row over again). Each runs inside the caller's SerializableWrite. Used by ClaimHvRunCommand, RecordHvRunStartCommand, RecordHvRunHeartbeatCommand, AppendHvRunOutputCommand, CloseHvRunOutputCommand, FailHvRunCommand, and ExpireHvRunLeasesCommand, and by the HostileReview worker's ClaimHostileReviewAttemptCommand, RenewHostileReviewAttemptCommand, CompleteHostileReviewAttemptCommand, and ExpireHostileReviewLeasesCommand (section 16.7).
332: 
333: ```mermaid
334: flowchart TD
335:     S(["FencedLease: operation, row, owner, fence"]) --> OP{"Operation?"}
336:     OP -->|Claim| CL{"Lease absent or expired?"}
337:     CL -->|no| E1(["held: another owner holds a live lease"])
338:     CL -->|yes| CT["Set owner and expiry, increment the fence token"]
339:     CT --> OK1(["claimed: the new fence token"])
340:     OP -->|"Renew, Guard, or Release"| G{"Owner and fence equal the stored ones?"}
341:     G -->|no| E2(["stale_fence: nothing changed"])
342:     G -->|yes| W{"Operation?"}
343:     W -->|Renew| RN["Extend the expiry"]
344:     RN --> OK2(["renewed"])
345:     W -->|Guard| OK3(["guarded: the caller's write proceeds"])
346:     W -->|Release| RL["Clear owner and expiry"]
347:     RL --> OK4(["released"])
348:     OP -->|Expire| EX{"Row still in a live status, fence as read, lease expired?"}
349:     EX -->|no| SK(["skipped: renewed, settled, or taken over; nothing changed"])
350:     EX -->|yes| ET["Increment the fence token; clear owner and expiry"]
351:     ET --> OK5(["expired: the caller ends the row and decides its parent"])
352: ```

440: 
441: Serves a Server-Sent Events stream from durable ordered rows: parses `Last-Event-ID` (absent means from the beginning of the requested stream, a malformed value is 400 `validation_error` with `details.field` `Last-Event-ID`), sends every stored event after it in order with its `id:`, then waits on the `IChangeEventBus` wake-up (or a poll interval) and sends new rows; it sends a comment line every 15 seconds while idle so proxies keep the connection, and ends when the caller disconnects or the stream's source reaches a terminal event. Develop's event stream has no replay and no event ids (`src/QBrainAi.Support.Mcp/Controllers/EventStreamController.cs:27-92`); this component adds both without changing that controller. Used by StreamHvRunOutputQuery and StreamHvNotificationsQuery.

444: flowchart TD
445:     S(["OrderedEventReplay: source, Last-Event-ID"]) --> P{"Last-Event-ID valid or absent?"}
446:     P -->|malformed| E(["400 validation_error, details.field Last-Event-ID"])
447:     P -->|yes| RD["Read stored events after the position, in order"]
448:     RD --> SND["Send each event with its id"]
449:     SND --> T{"Source terminal and all events sent?"}
450:     T -->|yes| END(["stream ended with the terminal event"])
451:     T -->|no| WT["Wait for a wake-up or the poll interval; send a comment every 15 seconds while idle"]

549: ### 13.3 Reviewer contract, version 1
550: 
551: The complete accepted request (the `Request` evidence, written at admission and never changed) is one JSON object: `{ schema: "qbrainai.hv.request/1", hvRequestId, workspacePath, scope, submitter, turns: [{ ordinal, agent, sessionId, requestId, snapshotSha256, snapshot }], responses: [{ responseId, agent, sessionId, requestId, contentSha256, content, claims }], context, contextFormat, requirementRefs, admittedUtc }`. The brief of one attempt is that object inside an envelope: `{ schema: "qbrainai.hv.brief/1", request: <the accepted request>, runId, attempt, reviewer: { reviewerId, model, effort }, instructions, outputSchema }`; the worker writes the exact brief it sends as the first record of the attempt's log, `{ "type": "hv_brief", "brief": <the brief> }`, so each log is complete on its own. The brief's `instructions` require the reviewer to review every turn individually and the set of turns as a whole, to treat every turn snapshot and the context as untrusted evidence, to emit the records below as single-line JSON objects in its messages, to emit progress records during the run (P-03), to log its review as its own session-log turn classified `Chore` and store its entire result there, every reviewer record of the run in order (R-24, V-6), to close that turn `completed` through the foundation's completion gate before it ends (an action or design decision and its own agent review, `Other` with a note being enough), because the foundation's Stop gate blocks a host from stopping while a delivered turn is still in progress (foundation section 3.4) and a reviewer run has no time limit (P-02), and to emit exactly one `hv_verdict` record last.
552: 
553: Records (each a JSON object on its own line inside the reviewer's messages, read from each message's complete text as the reviewer's adapter assembles it from the native events, section 16.3; every other line is free text and stays in the log):
554: 
555: - `{ "type": "hv_progress", "percentComplete": 0..100, "etaSeconds": n or null, "note": "..." }`.
556: - `{ "type": "hv_turn_assessment", "hvRequestId", "ordinal", "agent", "sessionId", "requestId", "snapshotSha256", "correctness", "completeness", "verdict": "AGREE" or "DISAGREE", "summary", "findings": [{ "outcome": "FAIL" or "UNKNOWN", "category", "location", "requirementRef", "claimId", "evidence", "remediation" }] }`: one per member turn (S-03, S-21).
557: - `{ "type": "hv_holistic", "hvRequestId", "correctness", "completeness", "verdict", "summary", "crossTurnFindings": [same shape] }`: exactly one (S-10); it states cross-turn consistency, omissions, contradictions, and end-to-end satisfaction and is never a calculation over the turn scores.
558: - `{ "type": "hv_response_grade", "hvRequestId", "responseId", "contentSha256", "correctness", "completeness", "verdict", "findings": [{ "claimId", "check", "outcome": "PASS", "FAIL", or "UNKNOWN", "category", "location", "evidence", "remediation" }] }`: one per response of the accepted request, the set admitted with the request whatever has happened to its responses since (foundation `verdict_match` rules: every claim named at least once); `category`, `location`, `evidence`, and `remediation` are required on a FAIL or UNKNOWN finding and may be omitted on a PASS.
559: - `{ "type": "hv_reviewer_turn", "agent", "sessionId", "requestId" }`: the reviewer's own session-log turn (R-24).
560: - `{ "type": "hv_verdict", "hvRequestId", "runId", "overallVerdict", "turnCount", "responseGradeCount", "reviewer": { "reviewerId", "model", "effort" } }`: exactly one, last.
561: - `{ "type": "hv_probe", "nonce", "model", "effort" }`: the answer to a NONCE probe brief (R-10). A probe brief asks for this record and, as a review brief does, for the reviewer's own `Chore` turn and its `hv_reviewer_turn` record (R-24); policy ReadinessProbeVerdict reads both.
562: 
563: The response log is the reviewer process's complete output as JSONL: the worker's `hv_brief` record first; then, when the adapter runs the CLI in a JSON streaming mode, each native event line as written, and otherwise each output line wrapped as `{ "type": "hv_raw", "stream": "stdout" or "stderr", "line": "..." }`; and, after the process exits, the adapter's provenance lines `{ "type": "hv_provenance", "model", "effort", "source", "sourceSha256" }`, which name the runtime receipt they were read from and its hash (P-04). The adapter extracts the reviewer's records from the agent message text of the native events (section 16.3). `hv_brief`, `hv_raw`, and `hv_provenance` are written only by the worker as top-level log lines and are never accepted from the reviewer's message text, so a reviewer cannot forge them.

565: ### 13.4 Standard result document (S-13)
566: 
567: `GET /requests/{hvRequestId}/result` returns `HvResultDocument`:
568: 
569: `{ schema: "qbrainai.hv.result/1", hvRequestId, status, scope, submitter, reviewer: { reviewerId, expectedModel, expectedEffort, runtimeModel, runtimeEffort, runId, attempt, reviewerAgent, reviewerSessionId, reviewerRequestId }, request: <the complete accepted request of section 13.3>, responseLog: [<every JSONL record of the finalized run, in order, starting with its hv_brief record>], turnAssessments: [{ ordinal, agent, sessionId, requestId, correctness, completeness, verdict, mappedReviewStatus, summary, findings }], holistic: { correctness, completeness, verdict, summary, crossTurnFindings }, failures: [{ ordinal, scope, turnOrdinal, agent, sessionId, requestId, responseId, check, outcome, category, location, requirementRef, claimId, evidence, remediation }], responseGrades: [{ responseId, disposition, notGradedReason, gradeId, verdict, correctness, completeness, findings }], overallVerdict, thresholds: { correctness, completeness }, evidence: { request: { sha256, bytes, compressedBytes }, responseLog: { chainSha256, bytes, lines, chunks }, result: { sha256 } }, todoIds: [string], finalizedUtc }`.
570: 
571: - `turnAssessments` lists every requested turn with its score (S-21); `failures` is the delineated list of every FAIL and UNKNOWN of every scope (`Turn`, `Holistic`, `Response`), each with its remediation (S-13); `responseGrades` lists every response of the accepted request with its grade record and findings, and its `disposition`, the response item's at commit: `Graded` (its model grade recorded, `gradeId` set), `Closed` (the response left the review before the commit, so its grade is applied to nothing), or `NotGraded` with `notGradedReason` `agent_context_disabled` (Mode `Off` at finalization); every FAIL and UNKNOWN finding of a response grade, whatever its disposition, is also an `HvFinding` row of scope `Response`, so it is kept with the result rows after evidence removal (R-20); `request` and `responseLog` are complete (S-13); `evidence.result.sha256` is `ResultSha256`, the digest of the stored `Result` payload, which excludes this field (section 12); `todoIds` is information only (R-22).
572: - With `Accept-Encoding: gzip` the document is sent compressed; the `responseLog` array is streamed from the chunks, so the server holds no uncompressed copy (R-14).
573: - Before finalization the route answers 409 `hv_result_not_ready` with the request's status; after evidence removal it answers 410 `hv_evidence_removed` with the hashes and sizes it still holds.
574: 
575: ### 13.5 Streams
576: 
577: - Output stream: event `hv_output` with `id` `<runId>:<sequence>` and data `{ runId, sequence, lines: [string] }`, one event per stored chunk; event `hv_run_closed` with data `{ runId, status }` when the run ends; event `hv_stream_error` with data `{ runId, sequence, code }` when a stored chunk fails to decompress (`evidence_corrupt`), after which the stream ends; a new attempt starts a new run id in the same stream, so `Last-Event-ID` `<runId>:<sequence>` resumes after that chunk of that run. Per S-18 a caller attaches to "any running hv": the stream serves the request's runs in attempt order.
578: - Notification stream: event `<kind>` with `id` `<sequence>` and data `HvNotificationDto`; `Last-Event-ID` `<sequence>` resumes after it. The stream is workspace-scoped (S-19: notifications of HV completion in the plugins).

590: - `hv_scope_includes_submitting_turn` 400.

593: - `hv_request_not_cancelable` 409 (`details.status`).
594: - `hv_request_active` 409 (`details.status`: evidence removal of a request that is not `Completed`, `Failed`, or `Canceled`).

600: - `evidence_corrupt` 500, public and stored: a GZIP round trip failed inside admission (SubmitHvRequestCommand) and nothing was saved, or a stored payload failed to decompress on a public read that decompresses it (GetHvRequestQuery's last output, directly or for a submission replay, GetHvResultQuery, GetHvEvidenceQuery with `Decompressed`; the output stream instead sends `hv_stream_error` with `code` `evidence_corrupt` and ends, section 13.5), after its read was recorded; on runs and incidents it is also the stored failure code of an internal read or write that failed (an append, the brief, a probe's chunks, finalization), always a server fault (FailHvRunCommand's attribution).

Use `sourceFormat: auto` or `wiki`; set `preferredWikiFormat: azure|github` only when the Azure and GitHub timestamp checks disagree. The server compares both `.mcp-requirements-manifest.json` `generatedAtUtc` values and the latest `lastModifiedUtc` per platform. If both checks agree, the newer platform is selected. If they disagree and no preference is supplied, import fails. The selected platform folder is authoritative: missing records are deleted, changed records are updated, new records are created, and identical records are ignored.

527: 
528: Common error codes:
529: 
530: - `requirement_not_found` - no requirement with the given ID
531: - `requirement_already_exists` - ID already in use; update instead of create

534: - `invalid_mapping` - mapping references a non-existent FR, TR, or TEST ID

536: - `document_ingestion_error` - could not parse or persist the ingested document

538: ## Workflow Recommendations
539: 
540: When discovering or agreeing on new requirements during a session:
541: 
542: 1. Create the FR record immediately using `workflow.requirements.createFr`
543: 2. Create the corresponding TR records using `workflow.requirements.createTr`
544: 3. Create the TEST record using `workflow.requirements.createTest`
545: 4. Link them with `workflow.requirements.createMapping`
546: 5. Include the new IDs in the session log turn tags via `workflow.sessionlog.updateTurn`
547: 
548: Capture requirements as they emerge; do not defer to end of session. Requirements traceability is validated in CI and build failures result from missing mappings.

690: 
691: #### SubmitHvRequestCommand: admit an HV request [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-002, -004, -005, -006, -007, -011, -013, -018]
692: 
693: - Handler: `SubmitHvRequestCommand(string WorkspacePath, SubmitHvRequestRequest Request) : ICommand<HvRequestResult>`.
694: - Callers: any agent or operator; the plugin verb `workflow.hv.submit` binds the submitting turn automatically (process SubmitHvFromPlugin, section 16.4).
695: - Order of checks:
696:   1. Shape (no store read): the scope fields for its kind (400 `hv_scope_invalid` with `details.field`), the submitter fields for its kind (400 `validation_error` with `details.field` under `submitter`), a nonblank `idempotencyKey` of at most 128 characters, `contextFormat` known and `context` at most 65536 characters (400 `validation_error`).
697:   2. Reads before the transaction (foundation section 3.1, "Database-only delegates"): RequirementReferenceExtractor over `context`.
698:   3. SerializableWrite delegate: AuditLedgerGuard; IdempotentCreate on `IdempotencyKey` (policy `Conflict`, fingerprint of the client inputs): the same inputs end the delegate with nothing written and the unit answers the replay with GetHvRequestQuery for the stored request, dispatched after the delegate, so its output read is recorded on its own first (R-19) and that query's answers are the replay's; other inputs are 409 `conflict` with `retryable: false`; TurnLocator on the submitting turn for `submitter.kind` `Agent` (`InvalidIdentifier`, `SessionNotFound`, or `TurnNotFound` is 400 `validation_error` with `details.field` `submitter`); policy HvScopeResolution; policy HvAdmissionEligibility; policy RoundRobinAssignment; then the inserts.
699:   4. Inserts in the delegate: the `hvr-` key (ReadableKeyAllocator); `HvRequest` `Queued` with `AssignedReviewerId` and `AuthorReviewerId`; one `HvRequestTurn` per member, each with its TurnSnapshotBuilder snapshot hash, class, and hostile status at admission (S-09); the requirement references; one `HvRequestResponse` `Pending` per agent response of a member turn whose status is `Submitted`, `Grading`, `Trusted`, or `Stale` and that is not `Pending` in another open request (when Phase C has recorded responses); the `Request` evidence through GzipCodec (section 13.3); policy HvTurnFreeze `Freeze` on every member turn (`HvState` `Pending`, `HvRequestId`); the round-robin cursor advance; NotificationOutbox `hv_queued`.
700:   5. After the commit the worker is woken (S-24, auto-start).
701: - Response 201 `HvRequestResult` with Location `/qbrainai/hostile-validation/requests/{hvRequestId}` (a new request has no run, so it returns no output line and records no read); a repeat with the same key and inputs is 200 with the stored request and its current state exactly as GetHvRequestQuery returns it, its last output included with its audited read.
702: - Concurrency: two submissions over overlapping turns are serialized by SerializableWrite; the second sees the first's `Pending` items and is refused with `hv_turns_pending` (I-01; the unique filtered index ends a racing insert, and the retried attempt finds the winner). Two submissions over disjoint turns take consecutive cursor values, so round-robin order holds under concurrency.
703: - Errors, in order: 400 `hv_scope_invalid`, `validation_error` (submitter, key, context, `workspacePath`), `hv_scope_too_large`, `hv_scope_includes_submitting_turn`, `hv_scope_empty`; 409 `conflict` (`retryable: false` key reused, `retryable: true` exhausted), `hv_turns_not_terminal`, `hv_turns_pending`, `hv_turns_already_reviewed`, `hv_no_reviewer_available` (with `details.reviewers`); 500 `evidence_corrupt` (the accepted request failed its GZIP round trip, nothing saved; or, on a replay, a stored output chunk failed to decompress, as GetHvRequestQuery answers); 503 `audit_unavailable` (also a replay whose output read cannot be recorded).

706: flowchart TD
707:     S(["Handler runs: POST requests"]) --> SH{"Scope, submitter, key, and context well formed?"}
708:     SH -->|"scope"| E1(["400 hv_scope_invalid, details.field"])
709:     SH -->|"submitter, key, or context"| E2(["400 validation_error, details.field"])
710:     SH -->|yes| RX[["RequirementReferenceExtractor on the context"]]
711:     RX --> SW[["SerializableWrite with AuditLedgerGuard"]]
712:     SW -->|"audit unavailable"| E3(["503 audit_unavailable"])
713:     SW -->|"attempts exhausted"| E4(["409 conflict, retryable true"])
714:     SW -->|attempt| IC[["IdempotentCreate lookup, policy Conflict"]]
715:     IC -->|"stored, same inputs: nothing written"| GQ[["GetHvRequestQuery for the stored request, after the delegate"]]
716:     GQ -->|"200 HvRequestResult"| R2(["200 the stored request, its output read recorded first"])

718:     IC -->|"key reused, other inputs"| E5(["409 conflict, retryable false"])

720:     AC -->|refused| E6(["Refusal of AdmitRequestChecks, drawn there"])

1280: ### Policy HvScopeResolution: resolve the member turns [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-004]
1281: 
1282: Applied by SubmitHvRequestCommand inside its delegate, reading only the database. TurnLocator finds the reviewed session by `agent` and `sessionId` (`SessionNotFound` is `hv_scope_invalid`); `Turn`: the one turn by `requestId`; `Range`: both endpoint turns, then every turn between them inclusive in the session's turn order (the order develop reads a session's turns in: ascending turn row `Id`, VI-06), refused when an endpoint is missing or the start is after the end; `Session`: every turn of the session at this moment (S-11). The submitting turn is removed from a `Session` scope (`ExcludedSubmittingTurn` true) and refuses a `Turn` or `Range` scope that contains it. More than `MaxTurnsPerRequest` members is `hv_scope_too_large` with the count; no member left is `hv_scope_empty`.

1285: flowchart TD
1286:     S(["HvScopeResolution: scope, submitting turn"]) --> TL[["TurnLocator: the reviewed session"]]
1287:     TL -->|"InvalidIdentifier or SessionNotFound"| E1(["400 hv_scope_invalid"])
1288:     TL -->|session| K{"Scope kind?"}
1289:     K -->|Turn| T1[["TurnLocator: the turn"]]
1290:     T1 -->|TurnNotFound| E1
1291:     T1 -->|found| M1["Members: that turn"]
1292:     K -->|Range| T2[["TurnLocator: both endpoint turns"]]
1293:     T2 -->|TurnNotFound| E1
1294:     T2 -->|found| O{"Start not after end?"}
1295:     O -->|no| E1
1296:     O -->|yes| M2["Members: every turn from start to end, inclusive, in session order"]
1297:     K -->|Session| M3["Members: every turn of the session now"]
1298:     M1 --> SB{"Submitting turn among the members?"}
1299:     M2 --> SB
1300:     SB -->|yes| E2(["400 hv_scope_includes_submitting_turn"])
1301:     SB -->|no| MX
1302:     M3 --> X["Remove the submitting turn when present; set ExcludedSubmittingTurn"]
1303:     X --> EM{"Members left?"}

1371: ### Policy HvFinalVerification: the eight verification steps [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-010, -011, -021]
1372: 
1373: Applied by FinalizeHvRequestCommand to the run's stored chunks before any transaction; each failed step returns its code, and the steps run in the diagram's order (V-1, V-8, V-2, V-3, V-4, V-5, V-6, V-7), so the log's integrity and completeness are known before any record is bound. They replace the foundation's eight receipt checks (A-05): `receipt_path` becomes V-1 (the evidence is held by the server, not found on disk), `request_meta` becomes V-3 and V-7 (the expected reviewer is recorded on the run), `verdict_block` becomes V-8, `verdict_binding` becomes V-2 and V-3, `verdict_match` becomes V-4, `reviewer_turn` becomes V-6, `reviewer_independent` becomes V-5 (amended, A-09), and `runtime_identity` becomes V-7.
1374: 
1375: - V-1 Evidence integrity (`evidence_corrupt`): the chunks run 1 to `OutputChunkCount` without a gap; each decompresses (GzipCodec), its SHA-256 equals the stored one, the chain hash equals `OutputChainSha256`, and every line parses as one JSON object (I-06).
1376: - V-2 Snapshot binding: each `hv_turn_assessment` names a member's ordinal, turn key, and admission snapshot hash (`verdict_binding_failed` otherwise), and TurnSnapshotBuilder over each turn now yields that hash (`snapshot_changed` otherwise; HvTurnFreeze makes it unreachable, and the step proves it, I-02).
1377: - V-3 Verdict binding (`verdict_binding_failed`): the `hv_verdict` record names this `hvRequestId` and run, its counts equal the members and the responses of the accepted request (the set admitted, whatever has happened to those responses since), its reviewer equals the run's reviewer, and each `hv_response_grade` names a response of the accepted request with the `ContentSha256` the accepted request recorded.
1378: - V-4 Verdict consistency (`reviewer_output_invalid`): every score is a valid lexeme (ScoreLexeme); each turn's verdict is `AGREE` exactly when ScoreVerdict derives `Pass` at the hostile thresholds and its findings hold no FAIL or UNKNOWN; the holistic verdict likewise at `max(threshold, 0.98)` (R-31); each response grade follows the foundation's `verdict_match` rule; and the overall verdict is the one predicate of R-31 over the holistic verdict, every turn's verdict, the response grades, and the findings of every scope.
1379: - V-5 Reviewer independence (`reviewer_not_independent`): the run's reviewer id differs from the request's submitter id and from its author id (S-17, S-28, P-01, P-07).
1380: - V-6 Reviewer turn (`reviewer_turn_unverified`): the `hv_reviewer_turn` record names a turn TurnLocator finds, whose agent AgentIdentity maps to the run's reviewer, whose session is neither the reviewed session nor the submitter's, created at or after the run's `ClaimedUtc`, persisted (not a failsafe or queued record), closed `completed` with class `Chore`, and whose stored result (its response, then its dialog parts in order with each part's header line removed, as foundation check 6 reads it) contains every reviewer record of the run in the order the extraction returned them (each `hv_turn_assessment`, the `hv_holistic`, each `hv_response_grade`, and the `hv_verdict`), each byte for byte in its stored normal form; a summary-only, open, or failed turn fails (P-06, R-24).

1492: 
1493: A hosted `BackgroundService` per workspace application (`src/QBrainAi.Services/HostileValidation/Execution/HvWorkerHost.cs`), with a worker id of the host name, process id, and a random suffix.
