1516: ### 16.2 Process RunReviewerProcess: one attempt, live [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-008, -016]
1517: 
1518: Runs one claimed run. It builds the brief (section 13.3: the accepted request read from the `Request` evidence inside the run envelope, after AuditLedgerGuard `RecordRead` records that read, or the probe brief with its nonce, which reads no evidence); a refused read starts no process and ends the attempt without another write, so the lease expiry recovers it (W-02, W-12); a `Request` evidence that fails to decompress starts no process and fails the run with `evidence_corrupt` (FailHvRunCommand: a server fault, so a server incident and the reviewer unchanged, and the request through policy HvRetryDecision, whose attempts bound the retries, FR-MCP-HVPIPE-011-AC009). It asks the reviewer's adapter for the launch (section 16.3), starts the process with the workspace as its working directory and its plugin as a host session of its own (R-24), inside a containment bound to the worker process, so the reviewer and every descendant end when the worker dies, however abruptly (W-03; the containment, for example a process group or job object, is the adapter's, section 16.3), records the start (RecordHvRunStartCommand), and appends the `hv_brief` record as sequence 1. While the process runs it has four concurrent duties and no time limit (R-11, P-02): every line the adapter delivers goes into a buffer that is appended (AppendHvRunOutputCommand) when `OutputFlushBytes` accumulate; a flush timer appends a buffer that is not empty once `OutputFlushInterval` has passed since its first line, whether or not another line arrives, so a single line followed by silence is still appended within the interval (R-12); a heartbeat every `HeartbeatInterval` (RecordHvRunHeartbeatCommand) renews the lease and reads cancellation; and the process exit is awaited. `stale_fence` from any unit kills the process and ends the attempt without another write (W-03); `audit_unavailable` kills the process and ends the attempt (W-12); `evidence_corrupt` from an append (its round trip failed and nothing was saved) kills the process and fails the run with `evidence_corrupt` (FailHvRunCommand: a server fault, so a server incident and the reviewer unchanged, and the request through policy HvRetryDecision), and so does a non-retryable `conflict` from an append (a different batch under a stored sequence, or a sequence out of order), because the log's integrity can no longer be shown, and so does a 400 `validation_error` from an append, which only a worker defect can cause because the adapter wraps every line as one JSON object (section 16.3); a retryable `conflict` repeats the same unit call with the same sequence. Every FailHvRunCommand call of this process, and the worker host's shutdown call, goes through the nested activity FailAttempt, drawn once below: `failed` ends the attempt with the request's next state (or the probe's outcome) as that unit wrote it; a retryable `conflict` repeats the same call; `stale_fence` and 503 `audit_unavailable` end the attempt with no further write and the request as it was, which the lease expiry recovers (W-03, W-12); so no exit of this process names a request state that a refused write did not produce. A close answered 409 `conflict` with `details.field` `chunkCount` appends what is missing and closes again, and a retryable `conflict` repeats the close. Every append carries the records the adapter's extraction completed with that batch. On exit the remaining buffer is appended, the adapter's provenance lines are appended (section 16.3), and the run is closed (exit code 0, CloseHvRunOutputCommand, then FinalizeHvRequestCommand for a review whose request is `Finalizing`; a close that finds the request `CancelRequested` ends it `Canceled` instead, R-28; exit code 0 is not evidence of a review, R-11) or failed (FailHvRunCommand with `reviewer_exited_nonzero` and the exit code in its detail, or `reviewer_launch_failed` when the process never started). A cancellation read at a heartbeat kills the process and fails the run with `canceled`, which policy HvRetryDecision turns into the request's `Canceled` (R-28). Killing the process, here and in the diagrams, ends the reviewer's whole process tree, descendants included, also when the root process has already exited; and when the root exits while a descendant still holds its output pipes, the worker ends that descendant before it reads the output to its end. Without that, a descendant that outlives the reviewer would hold the run open forever, because no time limit ends a run (P-02); P14 is the same defect class in the plugin core (FR-MCP-HVPIPE-008-AC011).

1752: - Handler: `CompleteHostileReviewAttemptCommand(string WorkspacePath, string AttemptId, string WorkerId, long FenceToken, HostileReviewAttemptOutcome Outcome) : ICommand<HostileReviewAttemptResult>`; internal.
1753: - Delegate (SerializableWrite with AuditLedgerGuard), in this order: a request that already has an accepted result returns `alreadyAccepted` with it and writes nothing, whatever the caller's fence; then FencedLease `Guard` (`stale_fence`: nothing changed); the attempt must be `Claimed` or `Running`; when `Outcome.execution` is set, the execution row from it and, when no renewal set it (a reviewer that exited before its first renewal), the attempt's `ExecutionId`; then by outcome, each setting the attempt's `EndedUtc`: a success writes the result once (`AcceptedResultId`, `Verdict`, findings), makes the attempt `Succeeded` and the request `Completed`, and releases the lease (`accepted`); a failure, including one where no process started, makes the attempt `Failed` with its sanitized code, stores the outcome's sanitized diagnostics as the request's existing diagnostic rows (`HostileReviewDiagnosticEntity`, code and message, `src/QBrainAi.Storage/Entities/HostileReviewDiagnosticEntity.cs:23-31`), and releases the lease, and the request returns to `Queued` while counted attempts remain (`requeued`) and otherwise becomes `Failed` (`failed`); a cancellation makes the attempt `Canceled` with `worker_shutdown` (not counted) or `canceled` (counted) as the outcome says, and the request is decided as for a failure.
1754: - Results: `accepted`; `alreadyAccepted`; `requeued`; `failed`; `stale_fence`; 409 `conflict` (`retryable: true`); 503 `audit_unavailable`.

1594: ### 16.3 Reviewer adapter contract [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-001, -003, -008]
1595: 
1596: `IHvReviewerAdapter` (namespace `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.HostileValidation.Reviewers`), one implementation per reviewer id:
1597: 
1598: - `BuildLaunch(brief, reviewer)`: a `ProcessStartInfo` built as an argument list, never a shell string, with the brief on standard input or in a temporary file the adapter deletes after the run; the launch arguments come from one shared launch builder that develop's one-shot strategy also uses, so the per-CLI arguments of `OneShotCliAgentExecutionStrategy` (`AddCodexArguments`, `AddClaudeArguments`, `AddGrokArguments`, `AddClineArguments`, `OneShotCliAgentExecutionStrategy.cs:238-262`) are written once (DRY); processes start through the existing `IProcessSpawner` and `IProcessEnvironmentService` (`OneShotCliAgentExecutionStrategy.cs:18-21`), inside a containment the adapter creates at launch and binds to the worker process (for example a process group with a parent-death signal on Linux or a kill-on-close job object on Windows, settled in H1's contract step), so the reviewer and every descendant end when the worker dies, and so killing the run ends the whole tree even after the root has exited (W-03, FR-MCP-HVPIPE-007-AC008, FR-MCP-HVPIPE-008-AC011); develop's `DefaultProcessSpawner` starts an ordinary process and offers only an explicit kill (`src/QBrainAi.Common.AgentCli/DefaultProcessSpawner.cs:12-16,48-51`), so H1 adds the containment. The shared launch builder holds the one table of highest efforts of section 10 (P9). The reviewer runs behind a write barrier verified for its CLI (VI-03, probes of 2026-10-16): Codex `exec -s read-only` (a write attempt was refused by its sandbox), Grok `--permission-mode plan` (a write call was refused; a headless Grok run then ends `cancelled` at the first call that needs approval, so its launch allows the read tools a review uses), and Copilot `--available-tools` naming only read tools (write and shell tools are not offered at all). Claude's and Cline's plan modes are not accepted as barriers on that evidence (Claude's model declined before its barrier was exercised; Cline ran a shell command in plan mode), so Claude's launch restricts its tools structurally (`--tools`) and Cline stays unqualified until H1 proves a barrier. Whether each reviewer's plugin can still log its turn behind its barrier (the plugin writes host-session state and calls the server) is verified in H1 (VI-03, VI-04); a reviewer that cannot fails its NONCE (R-24).
1599: - Live lines (R-12, P8): standard output and standard error are read line by line as the process writes them (asynchronous line reads on the redirected streams), and each line is handed to the run's callback at once; nothing waits for the process to end.
1600: - `NormalizeLine(line, stream)`: a native JSON event line of a CLI run in a JSON streaming mode is kept as written; any other line becomes `{ "type": "hv_raw", "stream", "line" }`.
1601: - `ExtractReviewerRecords(lines)`: one pure function over a run's ordered native lines. It assembles each agent message's complete text by the CLI's event model (Grok's per-token `text` events, Copilot's `assistant.message_delta` events followed by the whole `assistant.message`, Claude's whole assistant messages, Codex's `agent_message` items, Cline's accumulated content) and returns, in message order, every line of that text that is exactly one JSON object of a reviewer record type of section 13.3; the fence lines of a fenced block are ignored, and a line holding other text beside a record is free text. The worker runs it as lines arrive and passes each batch's completed records to AppendHvRunOutputCommand; finalization runs it over the stored log; both get the same records (R-12). Record types the worker writes itself (`hv_brief`, `hv_provenance`, `hv_raw`) are never accepted from message text, so a reviewer cannot forge them.
1602: - `ReadProvenance(run)`: `hv_provenance` lines read from the CLI's own runtime receipt after the run (P-04), sources verified on 2026-10-16 (VI-01): for Codex, the thread's rollout `turn_context` (fields `model` and `effort`; observed `model` `gpt-6-astra`, `effort` `max`), the source the foundation's `runtime_identity` check reads (foundation section 6.3, check 8); for Claude, the session transcript under `~/.claude/projects` (the assistant message `model` and the request `effort`), written only when session persistence is on, so the launch never passes `--no-session-persistence`; for Grok, the session store `~/.grok/sessions/<cwd>/<sessionId>/` (`summary.json` `reasoning_effort`, and a model id that `chat_history.jsonl` names `grok-4.7-build` while the events name `grok-4.7`, so H1 pins the field V-7 compares); for Copilot, the run's own JSON stream (each call's `assistant.message.model` and `user.message.responsesReasoning.effort`; `--usage-output-file` holds the model only); for Cline, none, because its run records hold the model and only whether thinking was on, so V-7 and the NONCE fail closed (L-04, D-06).
1603: - Highest effort when none is configured: the verified values of section 10 (VI-08), never develop's one-shot constants (P9).

1605: ### 16.4 Process SubmitHvFromPlugin: the plugin verb [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-005, -020]
1606: 
1607: `workflow.hv.submit` in the PowerShell core (`plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1`): process BindVerbToTurn (foundation section 4.4) binds the invocation to its turn; the verb sends SubmitHvRequestCommand through the REPL with `submitter` that turn's key and `idempotencyKey` `hv-` followed by the first 32 lower-case hex characters of the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the whole invocation identity `{ submitter: { agent, sessionId, requestId }, scope, context, contextFormat }`, so the key has 35 characters whatever the length of the ids (within the 128 of section 12), two sessions with equal request ids get different keys, and a repeat of the same call is the same request. A created or stored request is reported with its id, status, and reviewer; the watcher needs no record of it, because a terminal notification carries the submitter's turn key (R-30, section 16.5). `hv_no_reviewer_available` is reported with the context S-16 asks for: each reviewer's enabled flag, readiness, and reason from `details.reviewers`, the open incident of each `Offline` reviewer (through `workflow.hv.incidents`), and the remedy text "after the cause is fixed, NONCE the reviewer: workflow.hv.nonce <reviewerId>". Every other refusal is reported with its code, final. A retryable answer (transport outage, 503, 409 with `retryable: true`) is reported with `retryable: true` and exit 1 and is not queued in the failsafe, because the same call with the same key can simply be repeated (the reviews' no-failsafe rule, foundation section 5.2).

1622: ### 16.5 Process WatchHvNotifications: completions into the plugin [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-017, -020]
1623: 
1624: Started by process StartHostSession (foundation section 4.4) for each host session and stopped by EndHostSession; one instance per host session (`sessions/<hostSessionKey>/hv-watcher.pid`, the arrival bridge's pattern). It runs the REPL streaming verb `workflow.hv.watchNotifications` with `Last-Event-ID` the `lastSequence` of `sessions/<hostSessionKey>/hv-notifications.yaml`. That one state file holds both `lastSequence` and the `inbox`, and every change to it is one atomic replace (temp file, flush, rename) under `hv-notifications.lock`. For each event the watcher writes, in that one replace, the new `lastSequence` and, when the event is `hv_completed`, `hv_failed`, or `hv_canceled` and its submitter session is this host session's MCP session (the submitter turn key the notification carries, section 12), an inbox entry keyed by the event's sequence; so a crash leaves either both or neither, and an event replayed after a crash is not added twice. Matching by the carried key needs no record of the submission, so a completion that arrives before the submit verb has returned is still inboxed. A disconnect reconnects with backoff from the recorded sequence, so nothing is missed (R-16). The prompt hook adds each undelivered inbox entry to the next prompt's context ("HV <hvRequestId> <status>, overall verdict <verdict>, sequence <n>; result: workflow.hv.result <hvRequestId>") and then marks it delivered in the same state file; a crash between the two repeats the entry at a later prompt, so delivery to the model is at least once, and the sequence makes a repeat recognizable (R-30). Plugins never call REST; the REPL holds the stream (R-30).

1646: ### 16.7 Process HostileReviewWorkerHost: the artifact worker of FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-003 (P1 to P3, D-02)
1647: 
1648: The HostileReview subsystem keeps its own bounded context, queue, entities, and surfaces (R-25); this section is the contract of its missing worker, fixed in H3. The requirements are the stored FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-002 and -003 with their texts unchanged; H0 writes the named tests below for their criteria, against mocks first, and H3 binds them to production.
1649: 
1650: - Host: a hosted `BackgroundService` of its own per workspace application (`src/QBrainAi.Services/HostileReview/Execution/HostileReviewWorkerHost.cs`), not HvWorkerHost, looping on a wake-up or `PollInterval`: ExpireHostileReviewLeasesCommand, then ClaimHostileReviewAttemptCommand until it returns null or `MaximumConcurrentReviews` attempts run, running each claimed attempt with a renewal every `RenewalInterval` (RenewHostileReviewAttemptCommand) until the reviewer exits, and then completing it. It reads the lease, renewal, and attempt options `HostileReviewWorkerOptions` already declares (`LeaseDuration`, `RenewalInterval`, `MaximumAttempts`, `PollInterval`, `MaximumConcurrentReviews`), which nothing reads today (P1). It shares with this pipeline only the reviewer adapters' launch builder, live-line path, containment, and provenance reader (section 16.3) and FencedLease (section 11.1).
1651: - Agent: the agent, model, and effort configured for hostile review when they are configured, and otherwise the pooled default agent with its default model and effort (FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-003 criterion 4, store text); P5's part for this worker removes the single-reviewer pin of `HostileReviewWorkerOptions.Validate` in H3 for this rule. HV's reviewer pool, round-robin, and NONCE do not apply.
1652: - No time limit: an artifact review runs until the reviewer exits, with no execution timeout (P-02, R-11); the options' `ExecutionTimeout` is not read. Liveness is the attempt's lease, renewed while the reviewer runs.
1653: - Storage (the subsystem keeps its entities and their single-column keys, R-25; in `src/QBrainAi.Storage/Entities/`): `HostileReviewAttemptEntity` (table `HostileReviewAttempts`, key `AttemptId` (128), with `WorkspaceId` and the root id `RequestId`, a foreign key to the request like the subsystem's execution and diagnostic rows, `HostileReviewExecutionEntity.cs:63-65`): `AttemptNumber` (int), `PoolJobId` (128), `ExecutionId` (128, null until the reviewer process starts; set by the first renewal after the start, or by the completion when the reviewer exited before any renewal), `Status` (16: `Claimed`, `Running`, `Succeeded`, `Failed`, `Abandoned`, `Canceled`), `LeaseOwner` (256), `LeaseExpiresUtc`, `FenceToken` (long), `ClaimedUtc`, `EndedUtc`, `FailureCode` (64, sanitized), `IsDeleted`; unique filtered (`WorkspaceId`, `RequestId`) where `Status` is `Claimed` or `Running`, one live attempt per request. `HostileReviewRequestEntity` gains `AcceptedResultId` (128, set once, a key of its own, with the request's existing `Verdict` and findings as the accepted result), `AttemptCount` (int), and `IsDeleted`; its `Status` takes `Queued`, `Running`, `Completed`, and `Failed`. The existing execution row (`HostileReviewExecutionEntity`) is the model execution, one per launched process.
1654: - Internal result types (`src/QBrainAi.Services/HostileReview/Execution/`): `HostileReviewAttemptClaim { attemptId, requestId, attemptNumber, poolJobId, fenceToken, leaseExpiresUtc }`; `HostileReviewRenewResult { leaseExpiresUtc }`; `HostileReviewAttemptOutcome { kind (Success, Failure, Canceled), execution, verdict, findings, failureCode, diagnostics, counted }` (the parsed result and sanitized diagnostics only; never an artifact, a prompt, or an output line; `execution` null when no process started); `HostileReviewExecutionMetadata { executionId, reviewerAgent, model, effort, sourceSurface, promptTemplateId, promptVersion, startedUtc, endedUtc, inputTokens, outputTokens }` (the columns of `HostileReviewExecutionEntity`, `src/QBrainAi.Storage/Entities/HostileReviewExecutionEntity.cs:10-61`, filled as the next item states); `HostileReviewAttemptResult { status (accepted, alreadyAccepted, requeued, failed), acceptedResultId }`; `HostileReviewSweepResult { abandonedAttemptIds }`.
1655: - Execution metadata (FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-003 criteria 1 to 3), produced by the worker for every launched process: `executionId`, created when the worker launches the process; `reviewerAgent` and `sourceSurface`, the selected agent and its adapter's id; `promptTemplateId` and `promptVersion`, the worker's prompt template; `startedUtc` and `endedUtc`, the process start and exit as the worker observed them; `model` and `effort`, the values actually used, read after the exit by the adapter's `ReadProvenance` (section 16.3, the source V-7 reads for HV, P-04), never the configured ones; `inputTokens` and `outputTokens` when the CLI reports them, otherwise null with the diagnostic `token_metadata_unavailable` (criterion 3: omitted with a diagnostic, never fabricated). Because criteria 1 and 2 record the model and effort actually used, an agent with no reviewer adapter (section 16.3 has one per reviewer id), or whose adapter has no provenance source for them (Cline today, L-04 and D-06), launches no process and completes the attempt as a failure with `runtime_identity_unavailable`, and a run whose provenance shows no model or effort completes as the same failure, with its execution id, agent, and times in the diagnostic and no execution row.
1656: - Identities, distinct as criterion 4 requires: the request (`RequestId`); one attempt per claim (`AttemptId`, with lease, fence, and attempt number); the AgentPool job that runs it (`PoolJobId`); one model execution per launched process (`ExecutionId`, which is the run id criterion 2 names, the execution row with model, effort, agent, prompt template and version, and times, criteria 1 to 3); and the one accepted terminal result (`AcceptedResultId`).
1657: - Storage boundary (FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-002 criterion 4): the worker assembles the prompt in memory from links it reauthorizes at dispatch, reads the reviewer's output lines only to parse the result, and stores neither the prompt nor any output line nor any artifact content: only normalized identity, type, version or content hash, the parsed result, and sanitized diagnostics reach queue rows, notifications, logs, receipts, or result metadata.
1658: - Links (P3): every artifact type FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-002 lists resolves through its supported workspace-scoped service, the stored hash is of the resolved content (never of its id), and the limits of criterion 4 refuse more than 64 links, an artifact over 1 MiB decoded, aggregate input over 8 MiB, or uninspectable content. A link that fails its reauthorization at dispatch (missing, unauthorized, stale, or ambiguous, criteria 1, 2, and 4), or whose resolved content now exceeds a limit, launches no process: the attempt completes as a failure whose sanitized diagnostic names the link's normalized identity and the code, and no link is ever left out of a prompt silently.
1659: - Execution: bounded at-least-once across process loss (an expired lease abandons the attempt and a new one runs, up to `MaximumAttempts` counted attempts); the reviewer runs contained with its worker (W-03), and a stopped attempt ends its whole process tree (section 16.2). 2247: 
2248: ```mermaid
2249: sequenceDiagram
2250:     participant W1 as Worker A, crashed
2251:     participant W2 as Worker B
2252:     participant H
2253:     participant DB
2254:     Note over W1: crashed while its run was Running, its process gone with it
2255:     W2->>H: ExpireHvRunLeasesCommand at its sweep
2256:     H->>DB: runs Claimed or Running with an expired lease
2257:     alt renewed, settled, or taken over by another sweep in the meantime
2258:         DB-->>H: skipped by FencedLease Expire, the request untouched

2260:         H->>DB: run Abandoned lease_expired, fence incremented, server incident, policy HvRetryDecision

2262:             DB-->>H: request untouched
2263:         else request CancelRequested
2264:             DB-->>H: request Canceled, turns released, responses closed, hv_canceled
2265:         else attempts left
2266:             DB-->>H: request Queued
2267:         else attempts exhausted
2268:             DB-->>H: request Failed, turns released, responses closed, hv_failed
2269:         end
2270:     end
2271:     H-->>W2: abandoned runs and Finalizing requests
2272:     W2->>H: FinalizeHvRequestCommand for each Finalizing request
2273:     W2->>H: ClaimHvRunCommand
2274:     opt worker A was alive but paused past its lease
2275:         W1->>H: any fenced write with the old fence
2276:         H-->>W1: stale_fence
2277:         W1->>W1: kill its process, end the attempt

2494: 
2495: Actors: Operator (through Director or the REPL), server. Trigger: the operator lists, inspects, enables, disables, or retunes a reviewer. Main flow: the operator lists the pool (ListHvReviewersQuery), reads one reviewer (GetHvReviewerQuery), and changes its enabled flag, strategy, agent path, model, effort, or concurrency with the state version it read (UpdateHvReviewerCommand); a change to the strategy, agent path, model, or effort makes the reviewer `Unverified`, and the worker NONCEs it (UC-HV-02). 2507: ### 18.3 UC-HV-02 NONCE a reviewer [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-003]
2508: 
2509: Actors: operator or any agent, HV worker, reviewer agent. Trigger: a reviewer is `Unverified` (startup or a launch change, requested by the worker) or `Offline` after its cause was fixed (requested by a caller, S-15). Preconditions: the reviewer is enabled. Main flow: the caller requests a NONCE (StartHvReviewerNonceCommand); the worker claims the probe (ClaimHvRunCommand), launches the reviewer with a probe brief carrying a fresh nonce (RunReviewerProcess), streams its output (AppendHvRunOutputCommand), appends the adapter's provenance, and closes the run (CloseHvRunOutputCommand); policy ReadinessProbeVerdict passes: the nonce is echoed, the provenance shows the expected model and effort, and the reviewer logged its own turn; the reviewer becomes `Online` with its resolved model and effort. Alternates: a probe already requested or running is reported without a second probe; a disabled reviewer is refused with 409 `hv_reviewer_disabled`; the probe fails (wrong nonce, wrong or missing provenance, no reviewer turn, launch failure, nonzero exit) and the reviewer stays or becomes `Offline` with an incident filed through triage (UC-HV-09); the probe's stored log fails its integrity check, a server fault, and a server incident is filed while the reviewer's readiness is unchanged; the reviewer is reconfigured while the probe runs, and the old probe, whether it closes, fails, ends with a shutdown, or loses its lease, changes nothing of the reviewer while the newer probe request waits (HvProbeOutcome); the worker dies during a probe of the current configuration and the sweep requests it again; the worker restarts after a probe settled on a server fault and requests no new probe until a caller asks. Postconditions: the reviewer's readiness reflects a probe of this moment (S-27); `reviewer_online` or `reviewer_offline` is announced. Invariants: only a passing NONCE moves a reviewer to `Online` (R-10).

2527: ### 18.4 UC-HV-03 Submit an HV request [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-002, -004, -005, -006, -013, -018]
2528: 
2529: Actors: model (through its plugin) or operator (through Director), any client, server. Trigger: a caller wants a turn, an inclusive range of turns, or a whole session reviewed (S-03, S-11). Preconditions: the turns to review are terminal; for an agent caller, its own turn is bound by the plugin (BindVerbToTurn). Main flow: the caller submits the scope, optional context in Markdown or YAML, and an idempotency key (SubmitHvRequestCommand); the server resolves the requirement references of the context (RequirementReferenceExtractor), resolves the members (HvScopeResolution: the session's turns at admission time for a session scope, without the submitting turn), checks that every member is terminal, not under review, and never reviewed (HvAdmissionEligibility), picks the next eligible reviewer round-robin, never the submitter, the author of the reviewed session, or an alias of either (RoundRobinAssignment, HvReviewerEligibility), snapshots every member without its review records (TurnSnapshotBuilder), stores the complete accepted request compressed (GzipCodec), freezes the members (HvTurnFreeze), announces `hv_queued`, and wakes the worker (auto-start, S-24). Alternates: the same key and inputs return the stored request as GetHvRequestQuery returns it, its last output read audited; the key with other inputs is a conflict; a malformed scope, a scope over the limit, a scope naming the submitting turn, or an empty session scope is refused (400); turns that are not terminal, under review, or already reviewed are refused with every affected turn listed (409); no reviewer is eligible and the request is refused with every reviewer's status, and the plugin adds the reviewers' open incidents and the NONCE remedy (409, S-16); a turn whose class is `Chore` and whose hostile review is `Unnecessary` is admitted and graded like any other (S-09); a turn has no self-review, or any self-review grade or status, and admission is the same (S-28); the audit ledger is unavailable and nothing is written (503, S-29). Postconditions: one `Queued` request with its members frozen `Pending`, its accepted request stored, and its reviewer assigned. Invariants: I-01, I-07, I-08, I-10.

Alternates: attempts are spent and the request fails, releasing its turns; triage is unreachable and the filing is retried at each sweep; a worker died and its expired leases are swept (ExpireHvRunLeasesCommand), its runs abandoned and fenced out; two sweeps read the same expired run, and the second skips it (FencedLease `Expire`), so the run is abandoned once and a newer attempt or a terminal request is never touched (HvRetryDecision); a graceful shutdown ends runs with `worker_shutdown`, which is not counted as an attempt; the audit ledger is unavailable and the failed run cannot be recorded until it returns, after which the lease expiry recovers it. 239: ### 7.2 Mandatory scope (locked 2026-08-13; operations versus requirements locked 2026-08-14)
240: 
241: Operator directive (verbatim intent): hostile validation must test for workspace rule violations, requirement violations, and the current plan holistically, in addition to the requested validation. Mandatory attack surfaces on every run:
242: 1. Requested validation: every implementer claim (pass, done, green, fixed, SHAs, test counts, receipts).
243: 2. Workspace rules: honesty, receipts, MCP-only TODO, session, and requirement storage when the workspace uses the MCP server, PowerShell only, no Python. BDPv4 and related directives pertain only to code and documentation in the scope of implementing the project. Phase order (requirements drive tests; tests before implementation) is caught by a hostile review between phases of plan implementation. Do not fail it solely by comparing FR `createdAt` to test or implementation file times after the slice is written. Do not apply BDPv4 to user-directed operations.
244: 3. Requirements: apply to project requirement work only (product features, implementation, claimed-complete plan steps). FR, TR, TEST, AC, and mappings are required there; missing FR, TR, or AC for claimed-complete implementation work is FAIL.
245: 4. Current plan holistically: when the implementer claims plan-step completion, check the plan's definition of done, blockers, amendments, and exit criteria. A user-directed operational action does not have to satisfy an unrelated plan's definition of done unless it claimed that plan step done.
246: 
247: Two work classes:
248: 1. Project implementation scope: product code, product tests, project documentation, and plan-step completion for that implementation. BDPv4 and related directives pertain only to this class. Missing FR, TR, TEST, or AC for claimed-complete implementation work is FAIL on surface 3.
249: 2. User-directed general actions: operator-ordered lab or operations work that is not a product requirement (for example: uninstall an obsolete package, back up a device, pair wireless ADB, take a screenshot, copy a store the operator named, remove a leftover launcher). These are not FR, TR, or TEST. Surface 3 must not FAIL for "no FR or TR for this uninstall" or equivalent.

If the operator explicitly directed the action, default to class 2 unless the implementer also shipped product code or claimed a plan or FR complete. Do not invent a requirements gap to punish class-2 work. If class-2 work is mixed with class-1 product changes in the same turn, score them separately and FAIL surface 3 only on the class-1 slice. What still applies to class-2 work: surface 1 (did they do the directed action, with receipts), surface 2 (honesty, receipts, look before delete, PowerShell, no Python, MCP-only storage; not BDPv4 for the operation itself), and surface 4 only if they claim an active plan step is complete.

257: ### 7.3 Score gate and the bar (locked 2026-09-10)
258: 
259: A hostile validation passes only when both its accuracy score and completeness score are at least 98 percent. Any individual score below 98 is a failure; OverallVerdict must be DISAGREE when either score is below 98, even if the FAIL and UNKNOWN counts are both zero. If a reviewer emits a verdict without numeric accuracy and completeness scores, the HV is incomplete: treat it as DISAGREE until scores are present and at least 98. The threshold is an acceptance threshold, not a target reviewers may game or inflate. A sub-98 score cannot authorize any goal, TODO, requirement, or plan done-state change: display it as a failure, remediate, and rerun.

261: 98/98 HV (accuracy and completeness) is the bar for a functioning system, not perfection. Never lower, skip, or approve below it; lower thresholds let real bugs through that later become blocking test failures. When rounds stop converging, fix the process, never the threshold. "98/98 is not perfection, it is functional." Never propose lowering it (added 2026-10-13, from the operator's ruling of 2026-10-09).

277: ### 7.5 Before every HV round
278: 
279: - Read the whole plan and every document under review end to end; targeted checks are not holistic. When the operator asks for a reconciliation or projection of problems before HV, present every projected problem to the operator and get confirmation before launching the review (added 2026-10-13, from the operator's rulings of 2026-10-12 and 2026-10-13).
280: - Run a structured what-if pass per requirement, not only a consistency check. Ask what observably happens under: crash, restart, or replay at each step; ordering and concurrency; boundary and malformed input; each host or plugin, including unsupported ones; lifecycle (clear, resume, end, terminal states); isolation (cross-workspace, cross-session, cross-agent); legacy and upgrade; operator-visible output. Where the plan does not state the outcome, add a valid AC tagged with the plan's phase or slice and a named test. Adding a valid AC is always a win.
281: - Chain rules together to find deadlocks: rules that each pass alone but together leave no accepted remedy.
282: - Diff against known-good anchors and ask "How did it deviate? How do we get back in line?": (1) the operator's verbatim decisions, (2) current working code and baseline-green behavior, (3) classic patterns such as idempotency keys, transactional outbox with at-least-once delivery and idempotent consumers (never claim exactly-once), write-ahead journal before mutation, optimistic concurrency. Justify any departure explicitly or return to the pattern.
283: - Check that every field set and code list is defined once and identically everywhere, every mapping edge is backed by a TEST statement and vice versa, and handoff and TODO metadata match the plan.
284: - Edit only between rounds, never while a round is running.
285: - Propagation audit: after changing any rule, field set, code, or outcome, search every place that states it (requirements, ACs, TRs, TESTs, wire contracts, use cases, the plan's phase or slice tasks, host tables, handoff, TODO) and update each one, or replace the copies with a reference to one canonical statement. In one review round, three of six findings were rules changed in one place and left stale elsewhere. Large edit batches need this audit most.
286: - Prefer a traceable key over content matching when pairing records (for example queue position or a shared id rather than a text hash); content can differ in representation between producers.
287: - Search before adding, and lint mechanically: before writing any new rule, grep the whole document for an existing rule on the same subject; a second rule is a contradiction even if each is fine alone (one round added a two-AC TEST rule beside an existing three-AC one). Check cross-reference classes (FR->TR->TEST mappings, which of the plan's phases or slices owns each named case, phase order) with a small script instead of waiting for the reviewer to find them one per round.

Guidance that only lives in memory gets skipped under time pressure.
289: - Phase-boundary audit: every test or AC you add must be allocated to the plan's phase or slice where everything it depends on already exists (server gate, review verbs, marker fields). A behaviour that ships before its dependency needs an explicit activation contract (for example a server-written capability) and an inert mode, including after a rollback. Check the dependency chain and the rollout order for each new case, not just the AC text.

291: ### 7.6 When findings come back
292: 
293: - Ask "What did I miss?", not only "How do I fix this?". Classify each finding (crash window, cross-session addressing, traceability drift, field-set drift, use case vs requirement contradiction, metadata drift, and so on) and sweep the whole artifact for siblings of each class before the next round.
294: - Verify each finding against source before acting.
295: - Separate implementer fixes from operator decisions, and batch operator decisions into one question.
296: - Recurrence signal: when one design area produces new findings in round after round, the problem is structural, usually a missing traceable key or a missing single source of truth. Stop patching. Diff the area against the known-good pattern (for example single writer, one ordered log, idempotency key), return to it, and delete the mechanism the patches added. One design area failed for five rounds until a single minter reading one ordered log replaced the patches.
297: - Indistinguishable inputs: when two histories produce byte-identical inputs (a redelivery of one event versus a separate event with equal fields), no derived key can separate them. Adding per-invocation state such as a counter or salt breaks idempotence instead. Run the what-if on both histories, then state the honest limit: fail closed under an existing rule, probe how often it happens, and document it. Never promise two invariants the inputs cannot support. Before a fix, check it against every invariant the old value satisfied (purity, retry reuse, the two-process tests), not only the finding it repairs.

299: ### 7.7 Writing fixes
300: 
301: - Fix the deficient requirement. Reconcile with existing requirements first, strengthen an existing AC second, create a new requirement only when the need is genuinely new.
302: - Do not add design mechanism (protocols, algorithms, crash choreography) to plan text. State the observable, testable outcome; the how belongs to the contract step of the plan's phase or slice.
303: - Make each fix minimal, then attack it yourself before the next round; fixes are the main source of new findings. Do not churn text that a prior round accepted.

305: ### 7.8 Design principle and coordination
306: 
307: - Always have a traceable relationship when coordinating two disparate entities: every record, event, or message carries the root ids of whatever it is a child of or depends on, so it is attributable on its own. A missing parent id is a design failure. Find the commonality first when relating something new to existing knowledge. Where an external format lacks the key, say so and compensate in your own records; never infer it silently.
308: - Coordinating with another agent: use one append-only channel with read-back verification (the global memory MEMORY-PROCESS-007 is that channel). Accept counters that expose real defects; fold refinements in only as minimal ACs. Each effort keeps its own required reviewer and gates; keep cross-effort dependencies acyclic and order-independent. A decision relayed by one agent may not satisfy the other agent's approval controls; the operator may need to state it to each agent directly.

Previous red-before-green descriptions were incorrect and were never a valid description of this process."

186: 1. Requirements drive tests. Start from the approved functional requirements, use cases, technical requirements, TEST requirements, and acceptance criteria. For parity ports, preserve the original test's inputs, assertions, boundary cases, errors, and side-effect checks; a matching test count alone does not establish parity.
187: 2. Write the tests and their independent mocks or scripted fakes before writing or changing the production implementation for that increment. Supply deterministic contract-derived fixtures and expected responses through the intended dependency boundary. Expected values must come from requirements or independently pinned original behavior, never from the implementation under test. A mock must exercise the test's actual assertions and relevant interactions; merely returning true or bypassing the asserted path is not validation.
188: 3. Prove that the tests discriminate correct and incorrect behavior. Run correct mock responses through every required assertion. Deliberately supply wrong mock responses, boundary values, omissions, exceptions, or interactions to prove that the corresponding assertions reject them. Capture these rejection checks as expected negative controls inside a passing test harness. These controls are evidence that the assertions work, not an acceptable failing unit suite or permission to begin production code with red tests.

Do not substitute NotImplementedException stubs, deliberately red production tests, or a claim of 'red observed' for this evidence.

3: ## Session Start
4: 
5: 1. Read `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` in the repo root for the current API key and endpoints.
6: 2. For specific operational steps (session bootstrap, session log turn workflow, and helper command sequence), follow `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml`.

13: ## Rules
14: 
15: 1. `templates/prompt-templates.yaml` (`default-marker-prompt`) is the source of truth for specific agent instructions. `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` is the rendered runtime instruction set.
16: 2. Keep this file focused on durable workspace policy and conventions; avoid duplicating marker-file operational procedures.
17: 3. Use helper modules for session log and TODO operations. Do not make raw API calls.
18: 4. Persist session log updates immediately after each meaningful change (turn creation, action append, decision, requirement, blocker, file/context update). Do not defer saves.
19: 5. Capture rich turn detail: interpretation, response, status, actions (type/status/filePath), contextList, filesModified, designDecisions, requirementsDiscovered, blockers, and relevant processing dialog.
20: 6. Follow workspace conventions in `.github/copilot-instructions.md` for build, test, and architecture guidance.
21: 7. Use **only `pwsh.exe`** for shell commands and script execution; do not use `powershell.exe`.
22: 8. When you need API schemas, module examples, or compliance rules, load them from `docs/context/` or use `context_search`.
23: 9. Do not fabricate information. If you made a mistake, acknowledge it. Distinguish facts from speculation.
24: 10. Prioritize correctness over speed. Do not ship code you have not verified compiles and is logically sound.
25: 11. When writing session logs or other audit records, agents must identify themselves accurately using their real agent identity in Pascal-Case. Do not use placeholder, legacy, or misleading sourceType values.
26: 12. Never edit YAML by appending, replacing, or removing text lines. Deserialize the complete document into an object, mutate the object, serialize it, and save it. Use `plugins/core/lib-ps/yaml-object-mutation.ps1` for PowerShell work.

28: ## Byrd Test Gate
29: 
30: The canonical process is `docs/Development-Process-draft-v4.md`. To leave a Byrd implementation slice, the entire unit test suite for the current iteration and previous iterations must be completely passing. In this workspace, skipped tests are not passing tests: a validation gate requires zero failures and zero skips in the executed scope. Tests should directly track progress; deferred work belongs in MCP TODO/requirements state until that slice starts, not in skipped test placeholders.

32: ## Where Things Live
33: 
34: - `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` — connection details, API key, workspace config (regenerated on server start)

44: ## MCP Interaction via REPL Tools
45: 
46: Agents running inside `McpAgent` must use the 27 built-in tools instead of raw HTTP calls. See `docs/REPL-MIGRATION-GUIDE.md` for the full tool inventory and migration patterns.
47: 
48: Key rules:
49: - Use `mcp_session_*` tools for session log lifecycle (bootstrap, turns, history).
50: - Use `mcp_todo_*` tools for TODO CRUD (query, get, create, update, delete, plan, status, implementation).
51: - Use `mcp_requirements_*` tools for FR/TR/TEST queries.
52: - Use `mcp_client_invoke` for any sub-client method not covered by a dedicated tool (context search, GitHub, workspace, etc.).
53: - Do not make raw HTTP calls to `/qbrainai/*` endpoints when a tool is available.

66: ## Agent Conduct
67: 
68: You represent the workspace owner. Your work directly reflects the owner's professional reputation.
69: 
70: ### Honesty
71: 
72: - Do not fabricate information, capabilities, or results.
73: - Distinguish between facts, informed opinions, and speculation.
74: - Acknowledge mistakes immediately and correct them.
75: 
76: ### Correctness
77: 
78: - Prioritize correctness over speed.
79: - When uncertain, state your uncertainty and suggest verification steps.
80: - Prefer proven patterns over clever approaches unless directed otherwise.
81: - All code must have XMLDocs. All public APIs must be documented.
82: - Follow DRY, SOLID, and existing project conventions.
83: 
84: ### Decision Documentation
85: 
86: - Log every decision to the session log, including trivial ones.
87: - For each decision, document: what was decided, why, what alternatives were considered, what was rejected.
88: - Log design decisions as dialog entries with category "decision" and as session log actions with type "design_decision".
89: 
90: ### Professional Representation
91: 
92: - Every interaction is audited via the session log.
93: - Every commit must be correct, clean, well-described, and complete.
94: - Log all commits as actions with type "commit" (SHA, branch, message, files).
95: - Log all PR/issue comments as actions with type "pr_comment" or "issue_comment".
96: - Always sign PR comments using the same signature convention as commits, identifying the actual authoring agent.
97: 
98: ### Source Attribution
99: 
100: - Document all web sources in the session log as actions with type "web_reference" (URL, title, usage).
101: - Add source URLs to the turn's contextList array.
102: - Attribute external code in both the session log and code comments.
103: 
104: ## Requirements Tracking
105: 
106: When you discover or agree on new requirements during a session:
107: 
108: 1. Update the files in `docs/Project/`:
109:    - `Functional-Requirements.md` — append FR-MCP-* entries
110:    - `Technical-Requirements.md` — append TR-MCP-* entries
111:    - `TR-per-FR-Mapping.md` — append mapping rows
112:    - `Requirements-Matrix.md` — append status rows
113:    - `Testing-Requirements.md` — append TEST-MCP-* entries
114: 2. Include the requirement ID in your session log turn's tags.
115: 3. Capture requirements as they emerge. Do not defer to later.
116: 
117: ## Design Decision Logging
118: 
119: When a design decision is made:
120: 
121: 1. Log it as a session log dialog item with category "decision".
122: 2. Include: the decision, alternatives considered, rationale, and affected requirements.
123: 3. Add a session log action with type "design_decision".
124: 4. If the decision affects existing code or requirements, note what needs updating.
125: 
126: ## Session Continuity
127: 
128: At the start of every session:
129: 
130: 1. Follow the session-start checklist in `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml`.
131: 2. Read `docs/Project/Requirements-Matrix.md` to understand project state.
132: 3. If resuming interrupted work, review the last session's pending decisions.
133: 
134: At regular intervals during long sessions (~10 interactions):
135: 
136: 1. Follow marker-file update cadence and session logging requirements from `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml`.
137: 2. Ensure all design decisions are captured.
138: 3. Verify requirements docs are up to date.
139: 
140: ## Glossary
141: 
142: - **MCP** — Model Context Protocol, an open standard for tool-calling between AI agents and context servers.
143: - **Workspace** — a project directory registered with the MCP server. All workspaces share a single port; use the `X-Workspace-Path` header to target a specific one.
144: - **Marker File** — the `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` file at each workspace root. Contains connection details, auth token, and agent prompt.
145: - **API Key** — a per-workspace cryptographic token that rotates on each server restart. Required for all `/qbrainai/*` REST endpoints.
146: - **Streamable HTTP** — the MCP wire protocol transport at `/mcp-transport`. Carries JSON-RPC tool calls over HTTP POST with streaming responses.
147: - **Session Log** — an audit record of every agent interaction, stored per-session with full request/response history.
148: - **Context Pack** — an ordered set of document chunks retrieved by semantic + full-text hybrid search, scoped to the workspace.
149: - **Tool Bucket** — a GitHub repository containing tool manifest files, similar to a Scoop package bucket.
150: 
151: ## Response Formatting
152: 
153: - Do not use table-style output in responses.
154: - Use concise bullets or short paragraphs instead.

2903: The plan `PLAN-HVPIPELINE-001` derives from this section and cites it; the architecture is the authority (foundation, introduction). The delivery follows the operator's structure for this architecture (operator, 2026-10-11, verbatim: "I want the implementation plan to be organized into requirements as a phase, interfaces and code stubs as a phase for the entire plan, test-driven development unit tests with mocks as a single phase, and then you can begin implementation coding in a domain-driven design breakdown so that agents can be run in parallel for the coding.") and the Byrd Development Process v4 (S-33), and keeps the dependency order of the handoff: H0, H1, H2, H3, H7, H4, then H6 and H5, then independent validation. H6 precedes H5 because the plugin watcher and the client streams of H5 consume the streams H6 delivers, so no part of H5 ships before its dependency and none needs an activation contract (section 19.4).

163: - R-21 Self-review independence (S-28). No HV unit, policy, or process reads `agentReview`. The turn snapshot sent to a reviewer omits both review records (shared component TurnSnapshotBuilder), so a reviewer never sees a self-review grade. S-12 (a plugin list of missing agent reviews) is met by the foundation's Stop-gate remedy, which already lists each open turn's missing `agentReview` (foundation section 3.4, Stop gate, and `Get-CloseRemedy`, section 3.5.6), and is not an HV input. Reconciliation with the foundation's completion gate: HV admits only terminal turns (R-05), and the foundation's gate needs an `agentReview` status of `Pass`, `Fail`, or `Other` before a turn can close `completed` (foundation section 5.3, CompletionPolicy); that is a rule of closing a turn, not of HV, it is met by `Other` with a note as well as by a grade, and a turn closed `failed` or `canceled` needs no agent review at all; HV admission, execution, and verdict read none of it, and FR-MCP-HVPIPE-013 proves that every terminal turn is admitted and judged identically whatever its self-review.
164: - R-22 Verdict only (S-25). No HV unit writes TODO state. A result names the reviewed turns' `todoId` values for information only.
165: - R-23 Requirement references (S-14). The submitted context is stored as written (Markdown, YAML, or text, declared by `contextFormat`) and parsed for requirement references: FR, TR, and TEST ids of the form `<KIND>-<AREA>-<NNN>` with optional further dash-separated area segments, acceptance criteria written as `<FR id>-AC<NNN>` or `<FR id> ac-<n>`, and use cases by their store id or exact title. Each reference is resolved against the workspace's effective requirements and use cases and handed to the reviewer as a delineated list with its resolution status; an unresolved reference is listed as unresolved, never refused (shared component RequirementReferenceExtractor).
166: - R-24 The reviewer's own turn (P-06). The brief tells the reviewer to log its review as its own session-log turn, classified `Chore` so that its turn never needs an HV of its own (foundation completion policy: Chore needs no hostile review), and to store its entire result there. Finalization requires that turn to exist, to be persisted (not a failsafe or queued record), to have been created at or after the run's claim, to be closed `completed` as a `Chore`, and to contain every reviewer record of the run byte for byte in its stored normal form (V-6). A reviewer whose host cannot log turns fails its NONCE with `reviewer_turn_logging_unsupported`. The reviewer's plugin runs as a host session of its own: a review or probe run never reads or changes the plugin state or the session-log session of a live session of the same agent in the workspace (FR-MCP-HVPIPE-008-AC008), which matters because a reviewer starts in the workspace (section 16.2) and Grok's headless hooks write their host state under the working directory's `.mcpServer/grok/` (VI-04).
167: - R-25 The HostileReview subsystem stays separate. FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-001 to -006 (its queue, artifact links, findings, and query surface) are not changed by this amendment, as the foundation already states (foundation section 5.4); the problems found in it (section 21, P1 to P3) are tracked in REMED-HVPIPELINE-001. It stays separate (D-02, settled): it reviews artifacts (TODO, FR/TR/TEST, plans, files, commits; FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-002) while this pipeline reviews session turns (S-03), the approved foundation keeps it separate, and consolidating it is scope the operator has not named. Its missing worker (P1) has its own contract (section 16.7) and shares only the execution primitives that fit it (the reviewer adapters' launch builder, live-line path, containment, and provenance reader, and FencedLease), so reviewer execution exists once (the DRY ruling); nothing of this pipeline's evidence model applies to it, because FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-002 forbids storing a raw artifact or an assembled prompt.

2616: ### 18.9 UC-HV-08 Cancel an HV [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-008]
2617: 
2618: Actors: any caller (S-18, no roles). Main flow: the caller cancels (CancelHvRequestCommand); a `Queued` request is canceled at once and its turns released; a `Running` request becomes `CancelRequested`, the worker reads it at its next heartbeat, stops the reviewer, and the request becomes `Canceled` with its turns released. Alternates: the request is already `CancelRequested` or `Canceled` and nothing changes; it is `Finalizing`, `Completed`, or `Failed` and the cancel is refused (409); the reviewer exits with code 0 before the next heartbeat, and the close finds the cancel and ends the request `Canceled` instead of finalizing it (CloseHvRunOutputCommand, R-28); the run fails before the next heartbeat, and the failure ends the request `Canceled` (FailHvRunCommand, HvRetryDecision); the worker died and the lease expiry completes the cancel (ExpireHvRunLeasesCommand). Postconditions: a canceled request's turns are writable again; nothing of an unfinished review is recorded on them. Invariants: I-04.

1753: - Delegate (SerializableWrite with AuditLedgerGuard), in this order: a request that already has an accepted result returns `alreadyAccepted` with it and writes nothing, whatever the caller's fence; then FencedLease `Guard` (`stale_fence`: nothing changed); the attempt must be `Claimed` or `Running`; when `Outcome.execution` is set, the execution row from it and, when no renewal set it (a reviewer that exited before its first renewal), the attempt's `ExecutionId`; then by outcome, each setting the attempt's `EndedUtc`: a success writes the result once (`AcceptedResultId`, `Verdict`, findings), makes the attempt `Succeeded` and the request `Completed`, and releases the lease (`accepted`); a failure, including one where no process started, makes the attempt `Failed` with its sanitized code, stores the outcome's sanitized diagnostics as the request's existing diagnostic rows (`HostileReviewDiagnosticEntity`, code and message, `src/QBrainAi.Storage/Entities/HostileReviewDiagnosticEntity.cs:23-31`), and releases the lease, and the request returns to `Queued` while counted attempts remain (`requeued`) and otherwise becomes `Failed` (`failed`); a cancellation makes the attempt `Canceled` with `worker_shutdown` (not counted) or `canceled` (counted) as the outcome says, and the request is decided as for a failure.
1754: - Results: `accepted`; `alreadyAccepted`; `requeued`; `failed`; `stale_fence`; 409 `conflict` (`retryable: true`); 503 `audit_unavailable`.

192: ## 7. Lifecycles
193: 
194: ### 7.1 HV request
195: 
196: ```mermaid
197: stateDiagram-v2
198:     [*] --> Queued: SubmitHvRequestCommand, turns frozen Pending
199:     Queued --> Running: ClaimHvRunCommand, run attempt claimed
200:     Queued --> Canceled: CancelHvRequestCommand
201:     Running --> Queued: attempt Failed or Abandoned, attempts left
202:     Running --> CancelRequested: CancelHvRequestCommand
203:     CancelRequested --> Canceled: worker stops the process, the run closes or fails, or the lease expires
204:     Running --> Finalizing: CloseHvRunOutputCommand, output closed
205:     Finalizing --> Completed: FinalizeHvRequestCommand commits, turns Final
206:     Finalizing --> Queued: verification failed, attempts left
207:     Running --> Failed: attempts spent
208:     Finalizing --> Failed: verification failed, attempts spent
209:     Canceled --> [*]: turns released to None
210:     Failed --> [*]: turns released to None
211:     Completed --> [*]
212: ```
213: 
214: - `Queued` and `Running` hold the turns `Pending`. `Completed`, `Failed`, and `Canceled` are terminal and never change again (S-06, S-20). A request whose attempt fails returns to `Queued` with its assignment re-evaluated (R-07); with no eligible reviewer it stays `Queued`, its ETA `Unknown`, until a reviewer passes a NONCE or the request is canceled, so no work is lost to an outage.
215: - `CancelRequested` is not terminal: the request is canceled when the worker has stopped the process, when its run closes or fails first (CloseHvRunOutputCommand and FailHvRunCommand through policy HvRetryDecision, R-28), or when the lease of a dead worker expires.
216: 
217: ### 7.2 Run attempt
218: 
219: ```mermaid
220: stateDiagram-v2
221:     [*] --> Claimed: ClaimHvRunCommand, lease and fence
222:     Claimed --> Running: RecordHvRunStartCommand, process started
951:     PQ -->|"limit or offset out of bounds"| E2(["400 validation_error, details.field limit or offset"])
952:     PQ -->|page| R(["200 PageResult of HvIncidentDto"])
953: ```
954: 
955: ### 14.4 Execution (internal units, dispatched only by the worker host)
956: 
957: Every unit here is internal (R-29): its caller is process HvWorkerHost (section 16.1) or another unit of this section, never a route, tool, or client. Each returns a typed result to its caller; the codes in its list are those results, and none reaches a public surface.
958: 
959: #### ClaimHvRunCommand: claim the next probe or review [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-003, -007]
960: 
961: - Handler: `ClaimHvRunCommand(string WorkspacePath, string WorkerId) : ICommand<HvRunClaim?>`; `HvRunClaim { runId, kind, reviewerId, attempt, fenceToken, leaseExpiresUtc, hvRequestId, expectedModel, expectedEffort, probeNonce }`.
962: - Delegate: AuditLedgerGuard; then, in this order: (1) a probe: the first enabled reviewer, in pool order, with `ProbeRequestedUtc` set and fewer active runs than its `MaxConcurrentRuns`: insert its `Probe` run (`hvprobe-` key, a fresh 32-byte random `ProbeNonce` in lower-case hex), FencedLease `Claim`, clear `ProbeRequestedUtc`, and set the reviewer's `LastProbeRunId`; (2) otherwise a review: the oldest `Queued` request (by `CreatedUtc`, then `HvRequestId`) whose assignee is eligible with capacity, or whose assignee is no longer eligible and for which policy RoundRobinAssignment finds an eligible reviewer with capacity (the reassignment is recorded on the request); insert its `Review` run (`hvrun-<hvRequestId>-<nn>`, `Attempt` = `AttemptCount` + 1), FencedLease `Claim`, set the request `Running` (with `StartedUtc` on the first attempt) and `AttemptCount` + 1, and append `hv_started`. Every run records, at claim, `ClaimedUtc` and the reviewer's `ConfigurationVersion`, `ExpectedModel`, and `ExpectedEffort`. With nothing claimable it returns null and writes nothing; a request whose turns are all frozen stays `Queued` while no reviewer is eligible (ETA `Unknown`, R-18).
963: - Concurrency: the request's state, version, and the one-live-run index are checked and written in the delegate, so two workers never claim one request (W-11).
964: - Results: a claim; null; 409 `conflict` (`retryable: true`, the worker tries again at its next poll); 503 `audit_unavailable`.
965: 
966: ```mermaid
967: flowchart TD
968:     S(["ClaimHvRunCommand: workerId"]) --> SW[["SerializableWrite with AuditLedgerGuard"]]
969:     SW -->|"audit unavailable"| E1(["503 audit_unavailable"])
970:     SW -->|"attempts exhausted"| E2(["409 conflict, retryable true"])
971:     SW -->|attempt| P{"An enabled reviewer with a requested probe and free capacity?"}
972:     P -->|yes| PR["Insert the Probe run with a fresh nonce; clear ProbeRequestedUtc; LastProbeRunId the new run"]
973:     PR --> L1[["FencedLease Claim"]]
974:     L1 --> R1(["probe claim"])
975:     P -->|no| Q{"Oldest Queued request whose assignee is eligible with capacity?"}
976:     Q -->|yes| RV
977:     Q -->|"no, assignee no longer eligible"| RR[["Policy RoundRobinAssignment"]]
978:     RR -->|"no eligible reviewer with capacity"| NX{"Another Queued request?"}
979:     NX -->|yes| Q
980:     NX -->|no| R0(["null: nothing claimable"])
981:     RR -->|"reviewer, reassignment recorded"| RV["Insert the Review run, attempt AttemptCount plus 1"]
982:     Q -->|"no Queued request"| R0
983:     RV --> L2[["FencedLease Claim"]]
984:     L2 --> RS["Request Running, AttemptCount plus 1, StartedUtc on the first attempt"]
985:     RS --> N[["NotificationOutbox: hv_started"]]
986:     N --> R2(["review claim"])
987: ```

1516: ### 16.2 Process RunReviewerProcess: one attempt, live [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-008, -016]
1517: 
1518: Runs one claimed run. It builds the brief (section 13.3: the accepted request read from the `Request` evidence inside the run envelope, after AuditLedgerGuard `RecordRead` records that read, or the probe brief with its nonce, which reads no evidence); a refused read starts no process and ends the attempt without another write, so the lease expiry recovers it (W-02, W-12); a `Request` evidence that fails to decompress starts no process and fails the run with `evidence_corrupt` (FailHvRunCommand: a server fault, so a server incident and the reviewer unchanged, and the request through policy HvRetryDecision, whose attempts bound the retries, FR-MCP-HVPIPE-011-AC009). It asks the reviewer's adapter for the launch (section 16.3), starts the process with the workspace as its working directory and its plugin as a host session of its own (R-24), inside a containment bound to the worker process, so the reviewer and every descendant end when the worker dies, however abruptly (W-03; the containment, for example a process group or job object, is the adapter's, section 16.3), records the start (RecordHvRunStartCommand), and appends the `hv_brief` record as sequence 1. While the process runs it has four concurrent duties and no time limit (R-11, P-02): every line the adapter delivers goes into a buffer that is appended (AppendHvRunOutputCommand) when `OutputFlushBytes` accumulate; a flush timer appends a buffer that is not empty once `OutputFlushInterval` has passed since its first line, whether or not another line arrives, so a single line followed by silence is still appended within the interval (R-12); a heartbeat every `HeartbeatInterval` (RecordHvRunHeartbeatCommand) renews the lease and reads cancellation; and the process exit is awaited. `stale_fence` from any unit kills the process and ends the attempt without another write (W-03); `audit_unavailable` kills the process and ends the attempt (W-12); `evidence_corrupt` from an append (its round trip failed and nothing was saved) kills the process and fails the run with `evidence_corrupt` (FailHvRunCommand: a server fault, so a server incident and the reviewer unchanged, and the request through policy HvRetryDecision), and so does a non-retryable `conflict` from an append (a different batch under a stored sequence, or a sequence out of order), because the log's integrity can no longer be shown, and so does a 400 `validation_error` from an append, which only a worker defect can cause because the adapter wraps every line as one JSON object (section 16.3); a retryable `conflict` repeats the same unit call with the same sequence. Every FailHvRunCommand call of this process, and the worker host's shutdown call, goes through the nested activity FailAttempt, drawn once below: `failed` ends the attempt with the request's next state (or the probe's outcome) as that unit wrote it; a retryable `conflict` repeats the same call; `stale_fence` and 503 `audit_unavailable` end the attempt with no further write and the request as it was, which the lease expiry recovers (W-03, W-12); so no exit of this process names a request state that a refused write did not produce. A close answered 409 `conflict` with `details.field` `chunkCount` appends what is missing and closes again, and a retryable `conflict` repeats the close. Every append carries the records the adapter's extraction completed with that batch. On exit the remaining buffer is appended, the adapter's provenance lines are appended (section 16.3), and the run is closed (exit code 0, CloseHvRunOutputCommand, then FinalizeHvRequestCommand for a review whose request is `Finalizing`; a close that finds the request `CancelRequested` ends it `Canceled` instead, R-28; exit code 0 is not evidence of a review, R-11) or failed (FailHvRunCommand with `reviewer_exited_nonzero` and the exit code in its detail, or `reviewer_launch_failed` when the process never started). A cancellation read at a heartbeat kills the process and fails the run with `canceled`, which policy HvRetryDecision turns into the request's `Canceled` (R-28). Killing the process, here and in the diagrams, ends the reviewer's whole process tree, descendants included, also when the root process has already exited; and when the root exits while a descendant still holds its output pipes, the worker ends that descendant before it reads the output to its end. Without that, a descendant that outlives the reviewer would hold the run open forever, because no time limit ends a run (P-02); P14 is the same defect class in the plugin core (FR-MCP-HVPIPE-008-AC011).
1519: 
1598: - `BuildLaunch(brief, reviewer)`: a `ProcessStartInfo` built as an argument list, never a shell string, with the brief on standard input or in a temporary file the adapter deletes after the run; the launch arguments come from one shared launch builder that develop's one-shot strategy also uses, so the per-CLI arguments of `OneShotCliAgentExecutionStrategy` (`AddCodexArguments`, `AddClaudeArguments`, `AddGrokArguments`, `AddClineArguments`, `OneShotCliAgentExecutionStrategy.cs:238-262`) are written once (DRY); processes start through the existing `IProcessSpawner` and `IProcessEnvironmentService` (`OneShotCliAgentExecutionStrategy.cs:18-21`), inside a containment the adapter creates at launch and binds to the worker process (for example a process group with a parent-death signal on Linux or a kill-on-close job object on Windows, settled in H1's contract step), so the reviewer and every descendant end when the worker dies, and so killing the run ends the whole tree even after the root has exited (W-03, FR-MCP-HVPIPE-007-AC008, FR-MCP-HVPIPE-008-AC011); develop's `DefaultProcessSpawner` starts an ordinary process and offers only an explicit kill (`src/QBrainAi.Common.AgentCli/DefaultProcessSpawner.cs:12-16,48-51`), so H1 adds the containment. The shared launch builder holds the one table of highest efforts of section 10 (P9). The reviewer runs behind a write barrier verified for its CLI (VI-03, probes of 2026-10-16): Codex `exec -s read-only` (a write attempt was refused by its sandbox), Grok `--permission-mode plan` (a write call was refused; a headless Grok run then ends `cancelled` at the first call that needs approval, so its launch allows the read tools a review uses), and Copilot `--available-tools` naming only read tools (write and shell tools are not offered at all). Claude's and Cline's plan modes are not accepted as barriers on that evidence (Claude's model declined before its barrier was exercised; Cline ran a shell command in plan mode), so Claude's launch restricts its tools structurally (`--tools`) and Cline stays unqualified until H1 proves a barrier. Whether each reviewer's plugin can still log its turn behind its barrier (the plugin writes host-session state and calls the server) is verified in H1 (VI-03, VI-04); a reviewer that cannot fails its NONCE (R-24).
1599: - Live lines (R-12, P8): standard output and standard error are read line by line as the process writes them (asynchronous line reads on the redirected streams), and each line is handed to the run's callback at once; nothing waits for the process to end.
1600: - `NormalizeLine(line, stream)`: a native JSON event line of a CLI run in a JSON streaming mode is kept as written; any other line becomes `{ "type": "hv_raw", "stream", "line" }`.
1601: - `ExtractReviewerRecords(lines)`: one pure function over a run's ordered native lines. It assembles each agent message's complete text by the CLI's event model (Grok's per-token `text` events, Copilot's `assistant.message_delta` events followed by the whole `assistant.message`, Claude's whole assistant messages, Codex's `agent_message` items, Cline's accumulated content) and returns, in message order, every line of that text that is exactly one JSON object of a reviewer record type of section 13.3; the fence lines of a fenced block are ignored, and a line holding other text beside a record is free text. The worker runs it as lines arrive and passes each batch's completed records to AppendHvRunOutputCommand; finalization runs it over the stored log; both get the same records (R-12).
