1516: ### 16.2 Process RunReviewerProcess: one attempt, live [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-008, -016]
1517: 
1518: Runs one claimed run. It builds the brief (section 13.3: the accepted request read from the `Request` evidence inside the run envelope, after AuditLedgerGuard `RecordRead` records that read, or the probe brief with its nonce, which reads no evidence); a refused read starts no process and ends the attempt without another write, so the lease expiry recovers it (W-02, W-12); a `Request` evidence that fails to decompress starts no process and fails the run with `evidence_corrupt` (FailHvRunCommand: a server fault, so a server incident and the reviewer unchanged, and the request through policy HvRetryDecision, whose attempts bound the retries, FR-MCP-HVPIPE-011-AC009). It asks the reviewer's adapter for the launch (section 16.3), starts the process with the workspace as its working directory and its plugin as a host session of its own (R-24), inside a containment bound to the worker process, so the reviewer and every descendant end when the worker dies, however abruptly (W-03; the containment, for example a process group or job object, is the adapter's, section 16.3), records the start (RecordHvRunStartCommand), and appends the `hv_brief` record as sequence 1. While the process runs it has four concurrent duties and no time limit (R-11, P-02): every line the adapter delivers goes into a buffer that is appended (AppendHvRunOutputCommand) when `OutputFlushBytes` accumulate; a flush timer appends a buffer that is not empty once `OutputFlushInterval` has passed since its first line, whether or not another line arrives, so a single line followed by silence is still appended within the interval (R-12); a heartbeat every `HeartbeatInterval` (RecordHvRunHeartbeatCommand) renews the lease and reads cancellation; and the process exit is awaited. `stale_fence` from any unit kills the process and ends the attempt without another write (W-03); `audit_unavailable` kills the process and ends the attempt (W-12); `evidence_corrupt` from an append (its round trip failed and nothing was saved) kills the process and fails the run with `evidence_corrupt` (FailHvRunCommand: a server fault, so a server incident and the reviewer unchanged, and the request through policy HvRetryDecision), and so does a non-retryable `conflict` from an append (a different batch under a stored sequence, or a sequence out of order), because the log's integrity can no longer be shown, and so does a 400 `validation_error` from an append, which only a worker defect can cause because the adapter wraps every line as one JSON object (section 16.3); a retryable `conflict` repeats the same unit call with the same sequence. Every FailHvRunCommand call of this process, and the worker host's shutdown call, goes through the nested activity FailAttempt, drawn once below: `failed` ends the attempt with the request's next state (or the probe's outcome) as that unit wrote it; a retryable `conflict` repeats the same call; `stale_fence` and 503 `audit_unavailable` end the attempt with no further write and the request as it was, which the lease expiry recovers (W-03, W-12); so no exit of this process names a request state that a refused write did not produce. A close answered 409 `conflict` with `details.field` `chunkCount` appends what is missing and closes again, and a retryable `conflict` repeats the close. Every append carries the records the adapter's extraction completed with that batch. On exit the remaining buffer is appended, the adapter's provenance lines are appended (section 16.3), and the run is closed (exit code 0, CloseHvRunOutputCommand, then FinalizeHvRequestCommand for a review whose request is `Finalizing`; a close that finds the request `CancelRequested` ends it `Canceled` instead, R-28; exit code 0 is not evidence of a review, R-11) or failed (FailHvRunCommand with `reviewer_exited_nonzero` and the exit code in its detail, or `reviewer_launch_failed` when the process never started). A cancellation read at a heartbeat kills the process and fails the run with `canceled`, which policy HvRetryDecision turns into the request's `Canceled` (R-28). Killing the process, here and in the diagrams, ends the reviewer's whole process tree, descendants included, also when the root process has already exited; and when the root exits while a descendant still holds its output pipes, the worker ends that descendant before it reads the output to its end. Without that, a descendant that outlives the reviewer would hold the run open forever, because no time limit ends a run (P-02); P14 is the same defect class in the plugin core (FR-MCP-HVPIPE-008-AC011).

Alternate flows: the mint call is retried or replayed and returns the same requestId; a doubly registered hook delivers the event twice and both deliveries get the same requestId (only on hosts whose nonce is a stable per-message id or the bridge's single ordered source; on copilot and classic cline a second registration is refused before any mint, and a second new equal-field invocation fails the host session closed under the equal-field rule (Set-SessionUnsupported), while a stored mint retry or failsafe drain reuses its nonce); the server is unreachable and a provisional `pending-<nonce>` turn is rebound on drain; an identical prompt sent again later is a new event and opens a second turn; background event is skipped (on a bridge host it keeps its queue position as an unminted system entry, so its `dequeue` delivers nothing); operator sends a message mid-turn, the arrival bridge mints its turn at enqueue without touching the running turn or the write target, the message is delivered (absorbed into the running turn, or dequeued) and from then on, while the earlier request is still open, an unqualified write is refused with `request_ambiguous` (D9) and the model names the requestId of each write; once the earlier request is closed, unqualified writes bind to the delivered request; the operator pulls a queued message back (`popAll`) before delivery, the request is withdrawn, and the stop gate asks the model to fail it; a verb without a host session key in a workspace with two live sessions is refused rather than guessed; a subagent's hooks fire and leave this session's turns unchanged; while two delivered requests are open an unqualified verb is refused with `request_ambiguous` and the model names the requestId (D9);
